# AI Vision Colour Sorting with the Niryo One (complete version)

**Lab guide (PDF):** `docs/AI_Vision_Colour_Sorting_Lab_Guide.pdf` (setup, safety, every step with questions, the report).

A camera finds coloured cubes in the pick zone, a trained classifier names their colour, and
the Niryo One sorts red, yellow and green cubes onto squares A, B and C. **All the code is
given.** Tasks: set it up, run every step on your station, measure the results against
`SPECIFICATION.md`, and explain how each part works (the parts marked `KEY PART`).
Before you start, read the lab risk assessment RA001650/2 (summarised in the lab guide).

## A. Setup (once, on the lab PC)

Open your PyCharm project from the labs (the one with `ApiTCP_Python_NiryoOne`), then open the
**Terminal** tab at the bottom of PyCharm. The prompt must start with `(.venv)` (the project's
virtual environment); if it does not, run `.venv\Scripts\activate`.

1. Robot client (skip if the folder `ApiTCP_Python_NiryoOne` is already in the project):

       git clone https://github.com/LSBU-Electronics-Lab/ApiTCP_Python_NiryoOne.git

   In PyCharm, right-click that folder > Mark Directory as > Sources Root.

2. This project:

       git clone https://github.com/RoboticsT411/VisionSortingMaster.git
       cd VisionSortingMaster

   (Without git: unzip this folder into the project instead and `cd` into it.)

3. Packages:

       pip install -r requirements.txt

4. Settings: open `config.py` and set `CUBE_SIZE_MM` to your cubes' side length.

5. Check:

       python progress.py

   It prints the progress list with nothing ticked.

Optional, voice commands: `pip install vosk sounddevice`, unzip a Vosk English model
(e.g. `vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15`) next to `voice_commands.py`, test with `python voice_commands.py`.

## B. Order to run

Run these one after another from the project folder. A window shows what to do next and which
key to press: click the window once before pressing a key; `Q` quits. `python progress.py`
shows what is done at any time. Results go to `results/`.

| # | Command | What you do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `python step1_lab5_positions.py` | Choose your robot; type the gripper orientation and the Lab 5 pick-up and drop positions for A, B, C at levels 1, 2, 3; test each; save |
| 2 | `python step1_tune_camera.py` | Click the picture, `A` auto-tune, `S` save, `Q` quit |
| 3 | `python mapping.py` | Self-test of the camera-to-robot mapping (prints OK) |
| 4 | `python step1_check_calibration.py` | Follow the checklist (4 ticks for A, B, C): click the centres of A, B, C; check each square with the robot (T, centre the gripper, Y: circles refit automatically); click A, B, C again to confirm, all within 5 mm. Then the ruler checks (R7) |
| 5 | `python step2_collect_data.py` | `B` saves the empty background; then one colour per scene, its number key (`1` red ... `8` white, `0` other). Minimum 30 images in 5 scenes for red, yellow, green, other |
| 6 | `python step2_collect_data.py --dataset dataset_lighting2` | A small second set in clearly different lighting (about 10 images per class) |
| 7 | `python step3_train.py` | Compares the models, chooses one, tests it once |
| 8 | `python step3_baseline_hsv.py --train` | Tunes the colour rule on the training images |
| 9 | `python step3_baseline_hsv.py` | Tests the colour rule (once) |
| 10 | `python step3_live_detect.py` | Live colours and confidence; `S` saves a screenshot. The robot does not move |
| 11 | `python step3_experiments.py` | Learning curve, leakage test, threshold curve, lighting shift |
| 12 | `python step4_sort_blocks.py --measure-offset` | Sorting with the robot; confirm each move with a key. First 5 picks guided, then at least 20 picks |
| 13 | `python trials_summary.py` | Your trials against the specification, with 95 % intervals |

Optional: `python explore_kmeans.py` (unsupervised k-means on your dataset),
`python test_wrist_turn.py` (checks the gripper turns the right way), step 4 with `--voice`.

**Safety (risk assessment RA001650/2):** keep at least 30 cm from the robot while it is powered
(also when checking the gripper), only the technician moves the arm by hand or connects power,
one PC per robot, and confirm a move only when nothing is in the way. To stop: `Q` (or `Esc`
in a guided pick), `Ctrl+C` in the terminal, or switch off the robot's power.

## C. Key parts to study and explain

| Step | File | Key part | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3 | `mapping.py` | `compute_homography()`, `apply_homography()`, `mapping_errors_mm()` | Camera pixel to robot x, y from the four markers |
| opt. | `mapping.py` | `correct_parallax()` | Corrects the cube-top position for the camera angle |
| 7 | `step3_train.py` | `candidate_models()`, `compare_and_choose()` | Models tried; train, measure, choose on validation |
| 8-9 | `step3_baseline_hsv.py` | `classify()` | A colour rule with no learning, to compare with the model |
| 11 | `step3_experiments.py` | the four experiments | Evidence about the model |
| 12 | `step4_sort_blocks.py` | `choose()`, `pick_and_drop()` | Which cube next; the robot moves (from the Lab 5 program) |

Other files: `config.py` (all settings; the only file you need to edit), `camera.py`,
`aruco_view.py`, `block_finder.py`, `colour_model.py`, `vision.py`, `robot.py`, `ui.py`,
`progress.py`, `voice_commands.py`.

## D. Updates

Staff may update the project during the term. Inside the project folder run:

    git pull

# Specification: AI vision colour sorting with the Niryo One

This is the specification your system must meet, as an engineer would receive it from a
client. Read it before you start. Your report shows, requirement by requirement, whether your
system meets it, with the evidence and its uncertainty.

## 1. Purpose and scope

The system sorts coloured cubes from the pick zone onto squares A, B and C with a camera and
the Niryo One arm:

| Colour | Goes to |
|---|---|
| red | square A |
| yellow | square B |
| green | square C |
| any other colour, or anything that is not a cube | stays in the pick zone |

A person places up to 9 cubes, of any colours, anywhere inside the pick zone (the white outline
on the camera picture), not touching each other. The robot sorts every red, yellow and green
cube onto its square, stacking up to 3 per square, and leaves the rest.

**Out of scope:** cubes touching each other, cubes outside the pick zone, stacks higher than 3,
and lighting darker than the lab with the blinds closed.

## 2. Requirements

Every requirement must meet its **minimum**. The **stretch** targets are for the higher grade
bands. "How it is measured" names the program that gives you the number.

| ID | Requirement | Minimum | Stretch | How it is measured |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Colour accuracy on red, yellow and green | ≥ 90 % | ≥ 97 % | `step3_train.py` test report ("Sorted colours only") |
| R2 | Colour accuracy on all classes | ≥ 80 % | ≥ 90 % | `step3_train.py` test report |
| R3 | Better than a hand-written rule | model beats your colour rule | by ≥ 10 points, explained colour by colour | `step3_baseline_hsv.py` against `step3_train.py` |
| R4 | Wrong-colour drops | 0 in 20 picks | 0 in 50 picks | `trials_summary.py` |
| R5 | Pick success (cube placed correctly) | ≥ 80 % of 20 picks | ≥ 95 % | `trials_summary.py` |
| R6 | Grip offset from the cube centre | ≤ 6 mm on average | ≤ 3 mm, with the gain from parallax correction shown | `step4_sort_blocks.py --measure-offset`, then `trials_summary.py` |
| R7 | Calibration accuracy | every ruler check within 5 mm | within 3 mm | `step1_check_calibration.py` |
| R8 | Time per cube | ≤ 30 s | ≤ 15 s | `trials_summary.py` |
| R9 | Skipped cubes of red, yellow or green | ≤ 15 % | ≤ 5 % | threshold curve (`step3_experiments.py`), checked by counting cubes left after a run |
| R10 | Other lighting | accuracy drops ≤ 15 points | ≤ 5 points, and how you achieved it | `step3_experiments.py` lighting shift |
| R11 | Safety | no collision; every move checked against the safe area and confirmed; risk assessment RA001650/2 followed | — | observation; the step 4 review |

## 3. Cost of errors and the confidence threshold

Not all mistakes are equally bad. This table ranks them by what it takes to put each one right:

| Error | What has to happen to fix it | Relative cost |
|---|---|---|
| Collision | Stop the session, inspect the robot, possibly repair it | never accepted: prevented by hard rules (R11) |
| Wrong colour dropped | Notice it, lift off up to 2 cubes above it, restack (about 60 s) | **10** |
| Cube falls off the stack | Put it back (about 30 s) | **5** |
| Gripper misses the cube | The robot returns empty; the cube is picked next cycle (about 15 s) | **2** |
| Cube skipped (confidence too low) | It stays in the zone; pick it later or by hand (about 5 s) | **1** |

The confidence threshold (`CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD` in `config.py`) decides between the two errors
it controls: a low threshold skips few cubes but drops more wrong; a high threshold drops
almost none wrong but skips more. Because a wrong drop costs 10 skips, choose the threshold
with the **lowest expected cost per cube**:

    expected cost = 10 × (fraction dropped wrongly) + 1 × (fraction skipped)
    fraction dropped wrongly = coverage × (1 − accuracy of kept)
    fraction skipped         = 1 − coverage

Coverage and accuracy of kept, for each threshold, come from your threshold curve
(`step3_experiments.py`). In your report, fill in this table from it and give your choice:

| Threshold | Coverage | Accuracy of kept | Dropped wrongly | Skipped | Expected cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.50 | | | | | |
| … | | | | | |
| 0.95 | | | | | |

Then check the chosen threshold against R4 and R9. If no threshold meets both, say so and
explain what would fix it (more data, better features, a different model).

## 4. System architecture

| Block | File | Input → output | Units and frame | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Camera | `camera.py` | — → colour image | pixels | given |
| Marker detection | `aruco_view.py` | image → marker centres | pixels | given |
| Mapping | `mapping.py` | marker pixels and robot positions → homography; pixel → robot x, y | pixels → mm, robot base frame | given: **key part** |
| Object finder | `block_finder.py` | top-down image → cube candidates | top-down pixels | given |
| Classifier | `step3_train.py` | crop → colour and confidence | confidence 0 to 1 | given: **key part** (models and choice) |
| Parallax correction | `mapping.py` | x, y on the platform, height, camera position → corrected x, y | metres, robot base frame | given: **key part** |
| Decision | `step4_sort_blocks.py` `choose()` | detections and stacks → cube or none | — | given: **key part** |
| Motion | `step4_sort_blocks.py` `pick_and_drop()` | cube and Lab 5 positions → moves | metres, radians | given: **key part** |
| Safety | `robot.py` | every pose → allowed or refused | limits in `config.py` | given |

**Robot base frame:** origin at the base of the robot, x forward, y to the robot's left,
z up. All positions in the code are in metres in this frame.

## 5. Data plan

- **Classes:** red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple, pink, white, and other (not a cube).
- **Amount:** a target of about 100 images per class, from at least 20 scenes per class (one key
  press each). The minimum before training is 30 images in 5 scenes for red, yellow, green and
  other (training refuses to run below it, and the progress panel ticks step 2 when it is met).
  The other colours are optional: a colour with fewer than 3 scenes is left out of training.
- **Conditions:** at least two lighting conditions in the main dataset, for example blinds open
  and blinds closed. A separate small set in clearly different lighting, about 10 images per
  class, kept only for the lighting test (R10).
- **Labels:** one colour per scene. A second person checks about 10 % of each folder; record
  how many wrong labels were found.
- **Split:** by scene, 70 / 15 / 15 (given). Images of one scene are near-copies, so a split
  image by image would let the test set leak into training.

## 6. Evaluation plan

| Requirement | Evidence | Sample size | Uncertainty |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1, R2 | test report, used once | your test set (about 15 % of your images) | 95 % interval printed by `step3_train.py` |
| R3 | baseline and model on the same test set | same | compare the intervals: do they overlap? |
| R4, R5, R8 | robot trials | at least 20 picks | 95 % interval printed by `trials_summary.py` |
| R6 | offsets with and without parallax correction | at least 10 picks each | average and standard deviation |
| R7 | ruler checks | the 6 marker distances and at least 2 two-point checks | the largest difference |
| R9 | threshold curve, and cubes left after a run | validation set; one run of 9 cubes | — |
| R10 | lighting shift | the separate lighting set | 95 % interval |

**Small samples mislead.** 19 out of 20 is 95 %, but the 95 % interval is about 76 % to 99 %.
0 wrong out of 20 does not prove the wrong rate is 0: it can still be up to about 16 %.
`trials_summary.py` prints these intervals for you; use them when you say pass or fail.

## 7. Risks and mitigations

| Risk | Likelihood | Effect | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Camera knocked during a session | medium | every position wrong | ruler check at the start of each session; markers are re-detected in every frame |
| Sunlight changes the colours | high | accuracy drops | two lightings in the dataset; blinds closed for trials; R10 |
| Yellow confused with orange | medium | an orange cube dropped on B (wrong drop) | enough images of both; threshold from section 3 |
| Glare on a cube or marker | medium | missed cube or marker | camera auto-tune; matte markers |
| Wrong colour dropped | low | restack | threshold from section 3; R4 |
| Arm hits the camera arm or a stack | low | damage | pose limits, every move checked before the robot moves, a person confirms each move, power switch within reach |

## 8. Your report

Structure your report around this specification:

1. **Verification table**, first: for every requirement R1 to R11, the target, your result with
   its uncertainty, and pass or fail.

   | ID | Target (minimum) | Result | 95 % interval | Pass? | Evidence |
   |---|---|---|---|---|---|
   | R1 | ≥ 90 % | | | | test report |

2. **Design and implementation:** how each key part in section 4 works, why it is designed that way,
   and any change you made, with its effect measured.
3. **Experiments:** the four experiments from step 3.5 and the threshold table from section 3.
4. **Failure analysis:** every failed pick by cause (from `trials_summary.py`), with examples.
5. **Limitations and maintenance:** what your system cannot handle, and what someone would have
   to do to keep it working (for example after the camera is moved or the lighting changes).

"""
ArUco markers and the top-down view of the pick zone.

Four ArUco markers are fixed at the corners of the pick zone, in the same layout on every
station (MARKER_LAYOUT_MM in config.py). step1_check_calibration.py works out the robot x, y
of each marker centre from your Lab 5 positions of squares A, B and C.
In every camera frame the markers are found again, so the code always knows
how camera pixels map to robot coordinates, even if the camera is moved.

TopDownView uses that mapping (a homography) to:
  - warp the camera image into a flat top-down image of the zone,
    where 1 mm = PX_PER_MM pixels;
  - convert a pixel in that image into robot x, y in metres.
"""
import json

import cv2
import numpy as np

import config as cfg


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- markers
def get_dictionary():
    return cv2.aruco.getPredefinedDictionary(getattr(cv2.aruco, cfg.ARUCO_DICT))


def marker_image(marker_id, size_px):
    """Black and white image of one marker, for printing."""
    dictionary = get_dictionary()
    if hasattr(cv2.aruco, "generateImageMarker"):        # OpenCV 4.7 and newer
        return cv2.aruco.generateImageMarker(dictionary, marker_id, size_px)
    return cv2.aruco.drawMarker(dictionary, marker_id, size_px)


DETECTION_DEFAULTS = {"gamma": 1.0, "clahe": False, "threshold_constant": 7,
                      "window_max": 23, "min_perimeter": 0.03}


def load_detection_settings():
    """Image adjustments for marker detection saved by step1_tune_camera.py."""
    settings = dict(DETECTION_DEFAULTS)
    if cfg.CAMERA_SETTINGS_FILE.exists():
        settings.update(json.loads(cfg.CAMERA_SETTINGS_FILE.read_text()).get("detection", {}))
    return settings


class MarkerDetector:
    """Finds the ArUco markers. Only the image used for finding markers is
    adjusted (gamma, contrast); the colours the model sees are not changed."""

    def __init__(self, settings=None):
        self.configure(settings or load_detection_settings())

    def configure(self, settings):
        self.settings = dict(DETECTION_DEFAULTS, **settings)
        dictionary = get_dictionary()
        if hasattr(cv2.aruco, "ArucoDetector"):             # OpenCV 4.7 and newer
            params = cv2.aruco.DetectorParameters()
            params.adaptiveThreshConstant = float(self.settings["threshold_constant"])
            params.adaptiveThreshWinSizeMax = int(self.settings["window_max"])
            params.minMarkerPerimeterRate = float(self.settings["min_perimeter"])
            detector = cv2.aruco.ArucoDetector(dictionary, params)
            self._detect = detector.detectMarkers
        else:                                                # older OpenCV
            params = cv2.aruco.DetectorParameters_create()
            params.adaptiveThreshConstant = float(self.settings["threshold_constant"])
            params.adaptiveThreshWinSizeMax = int(self.settings["window_max"])
            params.minMarkerPerimeterRate = float(self.settings["min_perimeter"])
            self._detect = lambda img: cv2.aruco.detectMarkers(img, dictionary, parameters=params)
        gamma = float(self.settings["gamma"])
        self._lut = None
        if abs(gamma - 1.0) > 1e-3:
            x = np.arange(256) / 255.0
            self._lut = np.clip(255.0 * x ** (1.0 / gamma), 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
        self._clahe = cv2.createCLAHE(clipLimit=3.0, tileGridSize=(8, 8)) if self.settings["clahe"] else None

    def prepare(self, frame):
        """The grey image the detector actually looks at."""
        gray = cv2.cvtColor(frame, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
        if self._lut is not None:
            gray = cv2.LUT(gray, self._lut)
        if self._clahe is not None:
            gray = self._clahe.apply(gray)
        return gray

    def detect(self, frame):
        """Return {marker id: (u, v) pixel centre} and the raw corners for drawing."""
        corners, ids, _ = self._detect(self.prepare(frame))
        centres = {}
        if ids is not None:
            for c, marker_id in zip(corners, ids.flatten()):
                centres[int(marker_id)] = c.reshape(4, 2).mean(axis=0)
        return centres, corners, ids


def load_marker_positions():
    """Robot x, y (metres) of each marker centre, from calibration/markers.json."""
    if not cfg.MARKERS_FILE.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"{cfg.MARKERS_FILE} not found. Run step1_check_calibration.py first (step 1.5).")
    data = json.loads(cfg.MARKERS_FILE.read_text())
    positions = {int(k): np.array(v[:2], dtype=float) for k, v in data["markers"].items()}
    missing = [i for i in cfg.MARKER_IDS if i not in positions]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"markers.json has no position for marker(s) {missing}")
    return {i: positions[i] for i in cfg.MARKER_IDS}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- top-down view
class TopDownView:
    def __init__(self, marker_xy_m):
        self.marker_xy_m = marker_xy_m
        s = cfg.PX_PER_MM
        pts_mm = np.array(list(marker_xy_m.values())) * 1000.0
        self.x_min, self.y_min = pts_mm.min(axis=0)
        self.x_max, self.y_max = pts_mm.max(axis=0)
        self.width = int(round((self.y_max - self.y_min) * s)) + 1
        self.height = int(round((self.x_max - self.x_min) * s)) + 1

        # Robot (x, y) in mm  ->  top-down pixel (u, v).
        # u grows towards the robot's -y side, v grows towards the robot base.
        self.A = np.array([[0.0, -s, self.y_max * s],
                           [-s, 0.0, self.x_max * s],
                           [0.0, 0.0, 1.0]])

        self.H = None        # camera pixel -> top-down pixel
        self.fresh = False   # True only if all 4 markers were seen in this frame
        self.zone_mask = self._make_zone_mask()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ calibration
    def update(self, marker_centres):
        """Recompute the mapping from the markers seen in this frame."""
        ids = [i for i in cfg.MARKER_IDS if i in marker_centres]
        if len(ids) < 4:
            self.fresh = False
            return False
        from mapping import check_homography, compute_homography
        check_homography()                     # your functions must pass before they are used
        src = [tuple(map(float, marker_centres[i])) for i in ids]
        dst_mm = [tuple(map(float, self.marker_xy_m[i] * 1000.0)) for i in ids]
        H_cam_to_mm = compute_homography(src, dst_mm)          # KEY PART (mapping.py)
        if H_cam_to_mm is None:
            self.fresh = False
            return False
        self.H_mm = np.asarray(H_cam_to_mm, float)             # camera pixel -> robot mm
        self.H = self.A @ self.H_mm                           # camera pixel -> top-down pixel
        self.fresh = True
        return True

    def keep_out(self, points_xy_m, radius_mm=cfg.KEEP_OUT_RADIUS_MM):
        """Remove circles around these robot x, y points (squares A, B, C) from the pick zone."""
        r = int(radius_mm * cfg.PX_PER_MM)
        for x, y in points_xy_m:
            u, v = self.robot_to_topdown(x, y)
            cv2.circle(self.zone_mask, (int(round(u)), int(round(v))), r, 0, -1)

    def ready(self):
        return self.H is not None

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ images
    def warp(self, frame):
        """Top-down image of the pick zone."""
        return cv2.warpPerspective(frame, self.H, (self.width, self.height))

    def _make_zone_mask(self):
        """White where a cube may be picked: between the markers, a cube fully in the picture and
        never on a marker (see config.py: EDGE_MARGIN_MM, MARKER_KEEP_OUT_MM)."""
        pts = np.array([self.robot_to_topdown(*xy) for xy in self.marker_xy_m.values()])
        centre = pts.mean(axis=0)
        order = np.argsort(np.arctan2(pts[:, 1] - centre[1], pts[:, 0] - centre[0]))
        mask = np.zeros((self.height, self.width), np.uint8)
        cv2.fillPoly(mask, [np.int32(pts[order])], 255)
        shrink_mm = cfg.CUBE_SIZE_MM / 2 + cfg.EDGE_MARGIN_MM
        r = max(1, int(shrink_mm * cfg.PX_PER_MM))
        kernel = cv2.getStructuringElement(cv2.MORPH_ELLIPSE, (2 * r + 1, 2 * r + 1))
        # Pixels outside the image count as "not zone", so the edges shrink too.
        mask = cv2.erode(mask, kernel, borderType=cv2.BORDER_CONSTANT, borderValue=0)
        around_mm = (cfg.MARKER_SIZE_MM + cfg.CUBE_SIZE_MM) / 2 * np.sqrt(2) + cfg.MARKER_KEEP_OUT_MM
        for u, v in pts:
            cv2.circle(mask, (int(round(u)), int(round(v))), int(around_mm * cfg.PX_PER_MM), 0, -1)
        return mask

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ coordinates
    def robot_to_topdown(self, x_m, y_m):
        u, v, w = self.A @ np.array([x_m * 1000.0, y_m * 1000.0, 1.0])
        return u / w, v / w

    def topdown_to_robot(self, u, v):
        s = cfg.PX_PER_MM
        x_mm = self.x_max - v / s
        y_mm = self.y_max - u / s
        return x_mm / 1000.0, y_mm / 1000.0

    def camera_to_robot(self, px, py):
        from mapping import apply_homography
        x_mm, y_mm = apply_homography(self.H_mm, px, py)        # KEY PART (mapping.py)
        return x_mm / 1000.0, y_mm / 1000.0

    def robot_to_camera(self, x_m, y_m):
        u, v = self.robot_to_topdown(x_m, y_m)
        p = np.linalg.inv(self.H) @ np.array([u, v, 1.0])
        return p[0] / p[2], p[1] / p[2]

    def in_zone(self, u, v):
        ui, vi = int(round(u)), int(round(v))
        if 0 <= vi < self.height and 0 <= ui < self.width:
            return self.zone_mask[vi, ui] > 0
        return False

"""
Finds cube-sized objects in the top-down image of the pick zone.

This part is classical image processing, not machine learning. It answers
"where is something that could be a cube?" The trained model (step 3)
answers "what colour is it?", including "other" for things that are not
one of your cubes.

Two ways to separate objects from the platform:
  1. Background difference (default): compare with a picture of the EMPTY
     zone (calibration/background.png). Works for any cube colour.
  2. Colour rule (no background picture): keep strongly coloured pixels
     that are not the blue of the platform.
"""
from dataclasses import dataclass

import cv2
import numpy as np

import config as cfg


@dataclass
class Candidate:
    u: float              # centre, top-down pixels
    v: float
    angle_deg: float      # cube rotation in the image, -45 to +45 degrees
    size_mm: float        # estimated side length
    box: np.ndarray       # 4 corners, for drawing
    crop: np.ndarray      # CROP_SIZE x CROP_SIZE colour image of the cube


def load_background():
    if cfg.BACKGROUND_FILE.exists():
        return cv2.imread(str(cfg.BACKGROUND_FILE))
    return None


def foreground_mask(topdown, background=None):
    """White where something is on the platform."""
    blurred = cv2.GaussianBlur(topdown, (5, 5), 0)
    if background is not None and background.shape == topdown.shape:
        lab = cv2.cvtColor(blurred, cv2.COLOR_BGR2LAB).astype(np.int16)
        lab_bg = cv2.cvtColor(cv2.GaussianBlur(background, (5, 5), 0),
                              cv2.COLOR_BGR2LAB).astype(np.int16)
        diff = np.abs(lab - lab_bg)
        # Brightness (L) counts half, so shadows and light changes matter less than colour.
        distance = 0.5 * diff[..., 0] + diff[..., 1] + diff[..., 2]
        mask = distance > cfg.FOREGROUND_THRESHOLD
    else:
        hsv = cv2.cvtColor(blurred, cv2.COLOR_BGR2HSV)
        h, s, v = hsv[..., 0], hsv[..., 1], hsv[..., 2]
        platform_blue = (h > 90) & (h < 130)
        mask = (s > 90) & (v > 60) & ~platform_blue
    mask = mask.astype(np.uint8) * 255
    mask = cv2.morphologyEx(mask, cv2.MORPH_OPEN, np.ones((3, 3), np.uint8))
    mask = cv2.morphologyEx(mask, cv2.MORPH_CLOSE, np.ones((7, 7), np.uint8))
    return mask


def crop_around(image, u, v, half):
    """Square crop centred on (u, v), padded if it runs off the image."""
    padded = cv2.copyMakeBorder(image, half, half, half, half, cv2.BORDER_REPLICATE)
    ui, vi = int(round(u)) + half, int(round(v)) + half
    crop = padded[vi - half:vi + half, ui - half:ui + half]
    return cv2.resize(crop, (cfg.CROP_SIZE, cfg.CROP_SIZE), interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA)


def edge_angle(topdown, contour):
    """The cube's rotation (-45 to +45 degrees) from the direction of its straight edges.

    The outline of a cube seen from the side is not a square: the camera also sees one or two
    side faces, so a box fitted round the outline can be turned the wrong amount. The top
    and bottom edges of a cube all run at the cube's angle or at 90 degrees to it, so each
    edge pixel votes for its direction "modulo 90 degrees" (angle x 4), weighted by how
    strong the edge is. Returns (angle, agreement 0..1), or (None, 0) if there are no edges."""
    x, y, w, h = cv2.boundingRect(contour)
    pad = 6
    x0, y0 = max(x - pad, 0), max(y - pad, 0)
    x1, y1 = min(x + w + pad, topdown.shape[1]), min(y + h + pad, topdown.shape[0])
    gray = cv2.cvtColor(topdown[y0:y1, x0:x1], cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY).astype(np.float32)
    gray = cv2.GaussianBlur(gray, (3, 3), 0)
    gx = cv2.Sobel(gray, cv2.CV_32F, 1, 0, ksize=3)
    gy = cv2.Sobel(gray, cv2.CV_32F, 0, 1, ksize=3)
    region = np.zeros(gray.shape, np.uint8)
    cv2.drawContours(region, [contour - [x0, y0]], -1, 255, -1)
    region = cv2.dilate(region, np.ones((5, 5), np.uint8))      # include the outline itself
    mag = np.hypot(gx, gy) * (region > 0)
    theta = np.arctan2(gy, gx)
    c, s = float(np.sum(mag * np.cos(4 * theta))), float(np.sum(mag * np.sin(4 * theta)))
    total = float(np.sum(mag))
    if total < 1e-6:
        return None, 0.0
    angle = np.degrees(np.arctan2(s, c) / 4.0)                   # -45 to +45
    return float(angle), float(np.hypot(c, s) / total)


def find_cubes(topdown, view, background=None):
    """Return (list of Candidate, foreground mask)."""
    mask = foreground_mask(topdown, background)
    side_px = cfg.CUBE_SIZE_MM * cfg.PX_PER_MM
    expected_area = side_px ** 2
    contours, _ = cv2.findContours(mask, cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE)

    candidates = []
    for contour in contours:
        area = cv2.contourArea(contour)
        # Too small = noise. Too big = two touching cubes or a hand: skip it.
        if area < 0.4 * expected_area or area > 3.0 * expected_area:
            continue
        (u, v), (w, h), angle = cv2.minAreaRect(contour)
        if min(w, h) == 0 or max(w, h) / min(w, h) > 1.6:
            continue                       # not square enough to be a cube
        if not view.in_zone(u, v):
            continue                       # outside the safe pick zone
        angle = angle % 90.0               # a cube looks the same every 90 degrees
        if angle >= 45.0:
            angle -= 90.0
        edges, agreement = edge_angle(topdown, contour)
        if edges is not None and agreement > 0.15:
            angle = edges                  # straight edges are more reliable than the outline
        # Drawn box: a square the size of a cube, turned by the measured angle.
        box = cv2.boxPoints(((u, v), (side_px, side_px), angle))
        crop = crop_around(topdown, u, v, int(0.75 * side_px))
        size_mm = float(np.sqrt(area)) / cfg.PX_PER_MM
        candidates.append(Candidate(u, v, angle, size_mm, box, crop))
    return candidates, mask

import matplotlib

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

from colour_model import extract, list_dataset, load_images


def main():
    paths, labels = list_dataset()

    k = len(cfg.CLASSES)
    clusters = KMeans(n_clusters=k, n_init=10, random_state=0).fit_predict(X)

    lines = [f"k = {k}   adjusted Rand index = {adjusted_rand_score(labels, clusters):.3f} "
             f"(1 = clusters match your labels exactly, 0 = no better than chance)", ""]

"""
Camera-to-robot mapping and parallax correction.

KEY PARTS: the four functions marked "KEY PART" are the heart of this file and are
used by every step from 1.5 onwards. Study them: the guide asks you to explain each one.

1. The platform is flat, so a single 3 x 3 matrix, a HOMOGRAPHY, maps a camera
   pixel (u, v) to a point (x, y) on the platform in robot coordinates. It is
   found from the four markers: their pixel positions (from the camera) and their
   robot positions (worked out by step1_check_calibration.py).
2. The markers lie ON the platform, but the camera sees the TOP of a cube, which
   is higher. Seen at an angle, the top appears shifted away from the camera.
   correct_parallax() moves the position back, using where the camera is.

Check your work:
    python mapping.py           runs the self-checks on your functions
    python step1_check_calibration.py    measures your mapping against a ruler
"""
import numpy as np

import config as cfg


# =====================================================================================
# KEY PART 1 of 4: the homography from four (or more) point pairs
# =====================================================================================
def compute_homography(pixel_points, robot_points_mm):
    """Return the 3 x 3 homography H that maps camera pixels to robot coordinates (mm).

    pixel_points     list of (u, v): the marker centres in the camera image
    robot_points_mm  list of (x, y): the same markers in robot coordinates, mm
    Return a 3 x 3 numpy array, or None if it cannot be computed.
    Requirement: apply_homography(H, u, v) gives back each marker's (x, y) within 1 mm.
    """
    import cv2
    H, _ = cv2.findHomography(np.float32(pixel_points), np.float32(robot_points_mm))
    return H


# =====================================================================================
# KEY PART 2 of 4: use the homography
# =====================================================================================
def apply_homography(H, u, v):
    """Map one camera pixel (u, v) to robot coordinates with H. Return (x_mm, y_mm).

    Requirement: use homogeneous coordinates, so a point (u, v) becomes (u, v, 1).
    """
    x, y, w = H @ np.array([u, v, 1.0])
    return x / w, y / w


# =====================================================================================
# KEY PART 3 of 4: mapping error, to compare with your ruler checks
# =====================================================================================
def mapping_errors_mm(H, pixel_points, robot_points_mm):
    """For each point pair, the distance in mm between where H maps the pixel and where the
    point really is. Return a list of distances, one per point.
    """
    errors = []
    for (u, v), (x, y) in zip(pixel_points, robot_points_mm):
        mx, my = apply_homography(H, u, v)
        errors.append(float(np.hypot(mx - x, my - y)))
    return errors


# =====================================================================================
# KEY PART 4 of 4: parallax correction
# =====================================================================================
def correct_parallax(x_m, y_m, height_m, camera_m):
    """Correct the position of a point seen at a height above the platform.

    x_m, y_m   where the homography puts the point (robot coordinates, metres): this is
               where the camera's line of sight through the point meets the PLATFORM
    height_m   how high the point really is above the platform (e.g. the top of a cube)
    camera_m   (cx, cy, cz): the camera lens in robot x, y (metres) and its height above
               the PLATFORM (metres) - CAMERA_POSITION_M in config.py, which you measure
    Return the corrected (x, y) in metres: where the point really is.
    Requirement: a point straight below the camera does not move; a point at height 0 does not move.
    """
    cx, cy, cz = camera_m
    k = 1.0 - height_m / cz            # similar triangles along the line of sight
    return cx + (x_m - cx) * k, cy + (y_m - cy) * k


# =====================================================================================
# Given: self-checks
# =====================================================================================
_checked = set()


def check_homography():
    """Test compute_homography, apply_homography and mapping_errors_mm on a known mapping."""
    if "homography" in _checked:
        return
    true_H = np.array([[0.02, -0.55, 330.0], [-0.6, 0.01, 180.0], [0.00002, 0.0004, 1.0]])
    pixels = [(200, 120), (1080, 140), (1150, 650), (150, 620), (640, 380)]
    robot = []
    for u, v in pixels:
        x, y, w = true_H @ np.array([u, v, 1.0])
        robot.append((x / w, y / w))
    H = compute_homography(pixels[:4], robot[:4])
    if H is None or np.shape(H) != (3, 3):
        raise SystemExit("compute_homography() must return a 3 x 3 array")
    errors = mapping_errors_mm(H, pixels, robot)
    if len(errors) != len(pixels):
        raise SystemExit("mapping_errors_mm() must return one distance per point pair")
    if max(errors) > 1.0:
        raise SystemExit(f"Your mapping is off by up to {max(errors):.1f} mm on a test where the answer is known "
                         f"(the 5th point was not used to compute H). Check both functions.")
    _checked.add("homography")


def check_parallax():
    if "parallax" in _checked:
        return
    cam = (0.30, 0.0, 0.50)
    tests = [((0.30, 0.0, 0.025), (0.30, 0.0)),          # straight below the camera: no change
             ((0.20, 0.10, 0.0), (0.20, 0.10)),           # on the platform: no change
             ((0.20, 0.10, 0.025), (0.205, 0.095))]       # 5% of the way back towards the camera
    for (x, y, h), (ex, ey) in tests:
        rx, ry = correct_parallax(x, y, h, cam)
        if abs(rx - ex) > 1e-4 or abs(ry - ey) > 1e-4:
            raise SystemExit(f"correct_parallax({x}, {y}, {h}, camera {cam}) gave ({rx:.4f}, {ry:.4f}), "
                             f"expected ({ex:.4f}, {ey:.4f})")
    _checked.add("parallax")


def main():
    check_homography()
    print("Homography functions: OK (within 1 mm on a known test)")
    check_parallax()
    print("Parallax correction: OK")
    if cfg.CAMERA_POSITION_M is None:
        print("CAMERA_POSITION_M in config.py is not set yet: measure the camera lens position.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        main()
    except NotImplementedError as e:
        raise SystemExit(f"\nMissing: {e}\nCheck the function named in the message.")

"""
Project progress: which steps are done, worked out from the files each step saves.

    python progress.py          shows the checklist in a window and in the terminal

Every camera window shows the same checklist down its right side, and the
terminal-only programs print it when they start and finish. A step is ticked when
its result exists; the step you are running now is highlighted.
"""
import csv
import json
import time

import cv2
import numpy as np

import config as cfg

TRIALS_TARGET = 20

_cache = {"time": 0.0, "status": None}


def _trials():
    path = cfg.RESULTS_DIR / "trials.csv"
    if not path.exists():
        return 0, 0
    with open(path, newline="") as f:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(f))
    dry = sum(1 for r in rows if r.get("dry_run") == "True")
    guided = sum(1 for r in rows if r.get("dry_run") != "True" and r.get("guided") == "True")
    return dry, len(rows) - dry - guided          # guided picks (corrected by hand) are not trials


def _lab5_changed_since(snapshot):
    """True if the level-1 pick-up x, y of A, B or C moved since the calibration (test results don't count)."""
    if not snapshot or not cfg.LAB5_FILE.exists():
        return False
    try:
        pick = json.loads(cfg.LAB5_FILE.read_text())["pick"]
        return any(abs(pick[sq]["1"][i] - snapshot[sq][i]) > 0.0005 for sq in snapshot for i in (0, 1))
    except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError, IndexError):
        return True


def _calibration():
    """Done when step1_check_calibration.py confirmed the calibration (A, B, C all within 5 mm)
    and the Lab 5 positions have not been changed since."""
    if not cfg.MARKERS_FILE.exists():
        return False, "", False
    try:
        check = json.loads(cfg.MARKERS_FILE.read_text()).get("check")
    except ValueError:
        return False, "", False
    if not check:

# Click snapping: find the edges of the 25 mm hole near a click, and use its centre
# ======================================================================================
def snap_to_hole(frame, view, xy_m, px_per_mm=4.0):
    """xy_m: the click on the marker layout (metres). Returns the centre of the square hole found
    around it (metres) and a score, or (None, score) if no clear 25 mm square outline is there."""
    s = px_per_mm
    half = HOLE_MM / 2 + SNAP_MM + 4                                   # mm around the click
    x0, y0 = xy_m[0] * 1000 - half, xy_m[1] * 1000 - half
    size = int(2 * half * s)
    # patch pixel (u, v) <- layout mm: u along y, v along x, so the hole edges are horizontal/vertical
    P = np.array([[0.0, s, -y0 * s], [s, 0.0, -x0 * s], [0.0, 0.0, 1.0]])
    patch = cv2.warpPerspective(frame, P @ view.H_mm, (size, size))
    grey = cv2.GaussianBlur(cv2.cvtColor(patch, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY), (5, 5), 0).astype(np.float32)
    lab = cv2.cvtColor(patch, cv2.COLOR_BGR2LAB).astype(np.float32)
    edges = sum(np.abs(cv2.Sobel(c, cv2.CV_32F, 1, 0)) + np.abs(cv2.Sobel(c, cv2.CV_32F, 0, 1))
                for c in (grey, lab[:, :, 1], lab[:, :, 2]))           # brightness and colour edges
    side, ring = int(round(HOLE_MM * s)), max(2, int(round(1.5 * s)))
    tpl = np.zeros((side + 2 * ring, side + 2 * ring), np.float32)
    cv2.rectangle(tpl, (ring, ring), (ring + side, ring + side), 1.0, ring)
    tpl -= tpl.mean()
    score = cv2.matchTemplate(edges, tpl, cv2.TM_CCOEFF_NORMED)
    # Only hole centres within SNAP_MM of the click count (not a label or a cube further away)
    vv, uu = np.mgrid[0:score.shape[0], 0:score.shape[1]]
    near = np.hypot(uu + tpl.shape[1] / 2 - half * s, vv + tpl.shape[0] / 2 - half * s) <= SNAP_MM * s
    score = np.where(near, score, -1.0).astype(np.float32)
    _, best, _, (u, v) = cv2.minMaxLoc(score)
    cu, cv_ = u + tpl.shape[1] / 2, v + tpl.shape[0] / 2
    centre = np.array([(x0 + cv_ / s) / 1000, (y0 + cu / s) / 1000])
    moved = float(np.hypot(*(centre - np.asarray(xy_m)))) * 1000
    if best < 0.2 or moved > SNAP_MM:
        return None, best
    return centre, best

def turn_deg(R):
    return math.degrees(math.atan2(R[1, 0], R[0, 0]))


def rigid_fit(src, dst, stretch=False):
    """The turn R and shift t (no stretching) that best move the points src onto dst.
    stretch=True: also the same stretch in every direction (R then holds turn x stretch).
    Returns R (2 x 2), t (metres) and the distance left at each point, in mm."""
    src, dst = np.asarray(src, float), np.asarray(dst, float)
    sc, dc = src.mean(axis=0), dst.mean(axis=0)
    u, sv, vt = np.linalg.svd((src - sc).T @ (dst - dc))
    d = np.sign(np.linalg.det(vt.T @ u.T))              # a turn only, never a mirror image
    R = vt.T @ np.diag([1.0, d]) @ u.T
    if stretch:
        R = R * (sv[0] + d * sv[1]) / np.sum((src - sc) ** 2)
    t = dc - R @ sc
    left = np.linalg.norm(src @ R.T + t - dst, axis=1) * 1000
    return R, t, left


def place_layout(lab5, clicked):
    """lab5: {square: robot (x, y)} from step 1.1.  clicked: {square: (x, y) on the marker layout}.
    Returns a dict with "case": good / one_square / inconsistent / turned, and the numbers."""
    names = sorted(n for n in lab5 if n in clicked)
    R, t, left = rigid_fit([clicked[n] for n in names], [lab5[n] for n in names])
    out = {"names": names, "R": R, "t": t, "left": dict(zip(names, left)), "turn": turn_deg(R)}
    if abs(out["turn"]) > SWAPPED_TURN_DEG:
        out["case"] = "turned"
    elif max(left) <= FIT_MM and abs(out["turn"]) <= MAX_TURN_DEG:
        out["case"] = "good"
    else:
        # One square on its own? Place the layout with the other two and see if only that one misses.
        best = None
        for odd in names:
            rest = [n for n in names if n != odd]
            if len(rest) < 2:
                continue
            R2, t2, left2 = rigid_fit([clicked[n] for n in rest], [lab5[n] for n in rest])
            miss = float(np.linalg.norm(R2 @ np.asarray(clicked[odd]) + t2 - np.asarray(lab5[odd]))) * 1000

        self.commands = queue.Queue()
        self.state = "connecting"      # connecting / ready / moving / arrived / failed / closed
        self.status = "Connecting and calibrating the robot (about 30 s)..."
        self.robot = None

    def run(self):
        if not self.connect():
            return
        if NO_THREADS:                 # browser simulator: send() runs each command itself
            return
        while True:
            if not self.do(self.commands.get()):
                return

    def connect(self):
        try:
            from robot import NiryoRobot
            self.robot = NiryoRobot()
            self.robot.start()
            self.state, self.status = "ready", f"Robot {self.robot.ip} ready"
            return True
        except BaseException as e:                       # NiryoRobot.start() raises SystemExit on failure
            self.state = "failed"
            self.status = "Could not connect: " + str(e).strip().splitlines()[0][:90]
            return False

    def do(self, cmd):
        """Carry out one command. Returns False after "quit"."""
        try:
            if cmd[0] == "test":
                _, name, pose, z_safe = cmd
                self.state, self.status = "moving", f"Moving to {name}..."
                self.robot.learning_mode(False)                     # motors on to move
                self.robot.move_pose([pose[0], pose[1], z_safe] + pose[3:])
                self.robot.move_pose(pose)
                self.state, self.status = "arrived", f"Gripper at {name}"
            elif cmd[0] == "jog":                                   # a small correction while centring
                self.state = "moving"
                self.robot.move_pose(cmd[1])
                self.state, self.status = "arrived", "Adjusted"
            elif cmd[0] == "up":                                    # back up, then rest
                _, pose, z_safe = cmd
                self.state, self.status = "moving", "Moving back up..."
                self.robot.move_pose([pose[0], pose[1], z_safe] + pose[3:])
                self.robot.move_joints(cfg.SLEEP_JOINTS)
                self.robot.learning_mode(True)
                self.state, self.status = "ready", "Robot resting (sleep pose, learning mode on)"
            elif cmd[0] == "rest":                                  # L key: sleep pose, learning mode
                self.state, self.status = "moving", "Moving to the sleep pose..."
                self.robot.move_joints(cfg.SLEEP_JOINTS)
                self.robot.learning_mode(True)
                self.state, self.status = "ready", "Robot resting (sleep pose, learning mode on)"
            elif cmd[0] == "quit":
                self.robot.finish()
                self.state = "closed"
                return False
        except Exception as e:
            self.state, self.status = "ready", f"Move failed: {e}"
        return True

    def send(self, *cmd):
        if NO_THREADS:                 # browser simulator: run the command now (the picture pauses meanwhile)
            if self.state not in ("connecting", "failed", "closed"):
                self.do(cmd)
            return
        if cmd[0] in ("test", "jog", "up", "rest") and self.state not in ("connecting", "failed"):
            self.state = "moving"
        self.commands.put(cmd)

    def close(self):
        if self.state in ("failed", "closed", "connecting"):
            return
        if NO_THREADS:
            self.do(("quit",))
        elif self.is_alive():
            self.send("quit")
            self.join(timeout=30)

CHECK_COLUMNS = ["1 Clicked", "2 Fits camera", "3 Robot centred", "4 Confirmed", "5 Markers (optional)"]


def draw_mark(img, x, y, size, state):
    """state: "ok" (green tick), "bad" (red cross), "next" (orange outline), "todo" (empty), "skip",
    "later" (amber: not yet, the next step corrects it)."""
    colour = {"ok": GREEN, "bad": RED, "next": ORANGE, "todo": LIGHT_GREY, "skip": LIGHT_GREY,
              "later": ORANGE}[state]
    cv2.rectangle(img, (x, y), (x + size, y + size), colour, 3 if state == "next" else 2)
    if state == "ok":
        cv2.line(img, (x + 4, y + size // 2), (x + size // 2 - 1, y + size - 5), GREEN, 3, cv2.LINE_AA)
        cv2.line(img, (x + size // 2 - 1, y + size - 5), (x + size - 3, y + 4), GREEN, 3, cv2.LINE_AA)
    elif state == "bad":
        cv2.line(img, (x + 5, y + 5), (x + size - 5, y + size - 5), RED, 3, cv2.LINE_AA)
        cv2.line(img, (x + size - 5, y + 5), (x + 5, y + size - 5), RED, 3, cv2.LINE_AA)
    elif state == "skip":
        cv2.line(img, (x + 5, y + size // 2), (x + size - 5, y + size // 2), LIGHT_GREY, 2, cv2.LINE_AA)
    elif state == "later":
        cv2.circle(img, (x + size // 2, y + size // 2), size // 4, ORANGE, -1, cv2.LINE_AA)


def checklist_panel(width, rows):
    """rows: {square: [state for each of the four columns]}."""
    row_h, head_h, left = 34, 30, 120
    h = head_h + row_h * len(rows) + 8
    img = np.full((h, width, 3), 255, np.uint8)
    cv2.rectangle(img, (0, 0), (width - 1, h - 1), (200, 200, 200), 1)
    col_w = (width - left - 10) // len(CHECK_COLUMNS)
    cv2.putText(img, "Checklist", (10, 21), cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.6, (40, 40, 40), 2, cv2.LINE_AA)
    for c, name in enumerate(CHECK_COLUMNS):
        cv2.putText(img, name, (left + c * col_w, 21), cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.55, (40, 40, 40), 1, cv2.LINE_AA)
    for r, (square, states) in enumerate(rows.items()):
        y = head_h + r * row_h + 4
        done = all(s.partition("|")[0] in ("ok", "skip") for s in states[:4])
        cv2.putText(img, f"Square {square}", (10, y + 20), cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.6,
                    GREEN if done else (40, 40, 40), 2, cv2.LINE_AA)
        for c, state in enumerate(states):
            state, _, note = state.partition("|")                   # "state|note": a few words beside the box
            draw_mark(img, left + c * col_w + 4, y + 2, 24, state)
            note = note or {"skip": "skipped", "later": "fixed in step 3"}.get(state, "")
            if note:
                cv2.putText(img, note, (left + c * col_w + 34, y + 20), cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.45,
                            ORANGE if state in ("later", "next") else (110, 110, 110), 1, cv2.LINE_AA)
    return img

def placement_lines(p, robot_checked):
    """Title, colour and lines when the clicks and the Lab 5 positions do not fit together."""
    keys = "- R = click A, B, C again    - Q = quit"
    if p["case"] == "one_square":
        n = p["odd"]
        dx, dy = p["odd_shift_mm"]
        others = [s for s in p["names"] if s != n and s not in robot_checked]
        if n in robot_checked and others:
            # The square that "does not fit" is the one checked with the robot: the others are suspect
            o = " and ".join(others)
            return (f"{n} was centred with the robot, but {o} not yet: check {o} with the robot", ORANGE,
                    [f"- The camera compares A, B and C with each other. {n} now differs from {o} by {p['odd_mm']:.1f} mm.",
                     f"- The robot is the reference for picking, so {o} probably need the same correction.",
                     f"- Press T, then {others[0]}, then Y, and centre the gripper over {others[0]}.", keys])
        return (f"Square {n} does not fit with the others: its Lab 5 position is {p['odd_mm']:.1f} mm off", RED,
                [f"- Green circle = where the camera sees the centre of {n}. Red circle = your Lab 5 position for {n}.",
                 f"- Fix with the robot (best): press T, then {n}, then Y, and centre the gripper over {n}.",
                 f"- Or fix from the camera: press U (moves {n} by x {dx:+.1f} mm, y {dy:+.1f} mm; heights unchanged).",
                 f"- If your click on {n} was off instead, press R and click again.", keys])
    if p["case"] == "turned":
        return (f"Not calibrated: the layout would have to turn {p['turn']:.0f} deg to fit", RED,
                ["- The markers do not match MARKER_LAYOUT_MM in config.py (for example two markers swapped).",
                 "- Or the clicks were not on A, B and C in that order. Press R and click again.",
                 "- If it repeats, tell the technician.", keys])
    fits = ", ".join(f"{n} {p['left'][n]:.1f} mm" for n in p["names"])
    return ("Not calibrated: A, B and C do not fit the marker layout", RED,
            [f"- Distance left after the best fit: {fits} (needs {FIT_MM:g} mm or less, turn {p['turn']:+.1f} deg).",
             "- Fix with the robot (best): press T, then A, then Y, centre the gripper, Y. Then B, then C.",
             "- Circles refit after each square. When all three are centred with the robot, the fit is accepted.",
             "- If your clicks were off: press R and click A, B, C again on the centre of each hole.",
             "- Ruler checks: a wrong marker-to-marker length means MARKER_LAYOUT_MM does not match: tell the technician.",
             keys])


def saved_images(source):
    """True when the pictures come from saved images or a video, not from the camera (then no robot)."""
    return source is not None and not str(source).isdigit()


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--source", default=None, help="camera index, image, folder or video")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    print(__doc__)

    cam = Camera(args.source)
    detector = MarkerDetector()
    layout = layout_m()
    view = TopDownView(layout)                  # camera pixel <-> position on the marker layout (metres)
    try:
        squares = {s: np.array(xy) for s, xy in square_centres(load_lab5_poses()).items()}
    except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError) as e:
        print(f"Lab 5 positions needed first: {e}")
        squares = {}
    names = list(squares)

    def robot_checked():
        """Squares whose PICK level 1 position was confirmed with the robot (here or in step 1.1)."""
        try:
            tested = read_lab5_file()["tested"]
        except (TypeError, KeyError):
            return set()
        return {n for n in names if tested.get(f"pick {n} 1") == "ok"}

    pairs = list(combinations(cfg.MARKER_IDS, 2))
    pair_mm = {p: float(np.hypot(*(layout[p[0]] - layout[p[1]])) * 1000) for p in pairs}
    pair_result = {}                 # pair -> (ruler, diff, ok)

    cv2.namedWindow(WINDOW)
    cv2.setWindowTitle(WINDOW, f"Step 1.5 calibration - version {VERSION}")
    print(f"step1_check_calibration.py version {VERSION}")
    cv2.setMouseCallback(WINDOW, on_click)
    point_px, free_result = [], None # two-point measurement
    selected, typed = None, ""       # a pair, "free", or None; the ruler value being typed
    message, message_colour = None, BLUE
    offline = saved_images(args.source)                                   # saved images: no robot here
    stage = "click"                  # click -> robot -> confirm -> done, one after another; or "fix" / "failed"
    accepted = False                 # the fit from the clicks was accepted and saved
    queue_ = list(names)             # squares still to click in this round
    click_px = {}                    # round 1: pixel used for each square (the hole centre, or the click)
    clicked = {}                     # round 1: the same, on the marker layout (metres): kept for refits
    raw_px = {}                      # where you actually clicked, when it was moved to the hole centre
    confirm_px = {}                  # round 2 pixels
    missed = {}                      # square -> 1 after a click where the hole was not found
    placement = None                 # last fit of the layout to the Lab 5 positions
    place = None                     # (R, t) of the saved calibration: layout -> robot coordinates
    off_mm = {}                      # confirmation: distance of each square from its Lab 5 position
    robot_ok = set()                 # squares centred with the robot in THIS run (3rd tick)
    skip_robot = False
    tester = None                    # RobotTest, once T has been used
    test = None                      # robot check in progress
    last_shown = None
    loaded = None                    # time of a calibration loaded as already complete
    improved = None                  # step 5 result saved in markers.json
    marker_queue = []                # step 5: markers still to visit with the robot
    marker_robot = {}                # step 5: marker id -> robot x, y where the gripper was centred
    marker_skipped = set()
    report = []                      # step 5: lines shown after it

    # Already complete (step 1.5 ticked, Lab 5 unchanged)? Start on the finished checklist.
    status_15 = {row[0]: row for row in project_status(max_age=0)}.get("1.5")
    saved = load_saved_markers()
    if squares and status_15 and status_15[2] and saved is not None:
        data = json.loads(cfg.MARKERS_FILE.read_text())
        R0, t0, _ = rigid_fit([layout[i] for i in cfg.MARKER_IDS], [saved[i] for i in cfg.MARKER_IDS],
                              stretch=True)                     # step 5 may have saved a stretch
        place = (R0, t0)
        on_layout = data.get("squares_clicked_on_layout_mm", {})
        if all(n in on_layout for n in names):
            clicked.update({n: np.array(on_layout[n], float) / 1000 for n in names})
            placement = place_layout(squares, clicked)
        off_mm.update({n: float(v) for n, v in data["check"]["off_mm"].items()})
        robot_ok |= robot_checked()
        accepted, stage, loaded = True, "done", data.get("saved", "")[:16].replace("T", " ")
        improved = data.get("improved")
        print(f"Step 1.5 already complete (calibration saved {loaded}).")

    def to_robot(pt):
        x, y = view.camera_to_robot(*pt)
        return place[0] @ np.array([x, y]) + place[1]

    def to_camera(xy):
        lx, ly = np.linalg.solve(place[0], np.asarray(xy, float) - place[1])
        return view.robot_to_camera(lx, ly)

    def fit_and_save(p):
        """Accept a fit: save the marker positions and use it from now on."""
        nonlocal place
        save_markers(p, clicked)
        place = (p["R"], p["t"])
        print(f"Saved the marker positions to {cfg.MARKERS_FILE}")

    def refit():
        """Place the layout again from the round-1 clicks (after a Lab 5 position changed). No new clicks."""
        nonlocal squares, placement, accepted
        squares = {s: np.array(xy) for s, xy in square_centres(load_lab5_poses()).items()}
        placement = place_layout(squares, clicked)
        all_robot = robot_ok >= set(names)
        ok = placement["case"] == "good" or (all_robot and abs(placement["turn"]) <= MAX_TURN_ROBOT_DEG
                                             and max(placement["left"].values()) <= FIT_ROBOT_MM)
        print(f"Refit: {placement['case']}, fit " + ", ".join(f"{n} {v:.1f} mm" for n, v in placement["left"].items())
              + f", turn {placement['turn']:+.2f} deg" + (" (all squares centred with the robot)" if all_robot else ""))
        accepted = ok
        if ok:
            fit_and_save(placement)
        return ok

    def checklist():
        rows = {}
        fit_left = placement["left"] if placement else {}
        for n in names:
            c1 = "ok" if n in clicked or (loaded and n in off_mm) else ("next" if stage == "click" and queue_ and queue_[0] == n else "todo")
            if loaded and accepted:
                c2 = "ok"
            elif placement is None or n not in fit_left:
                c2 = "todo"
            elif stage == "failed":
                c2 = "bad"
            elif accepted or n in robot_ok:
                c2 = "ok"                    # fits, or its Lab 5 position was centred with the robot
            elif stage == "robot":
                c2 = "later"                 # not a failure: the robot check of this square corrects it
            else:
                c2 = "bad" if placement["case"] != "one_square" or placement["odd"] == n else "ok"
            if skip_robot:
                c3 = "skip"
            elif n in robot_ok:
                c3 = "ok"
            else:
                c3 = "next" if stage == "robot" and next_robot() == n else "todo"
            if n in off_mm:
                c4 = "ok" if off_mm[n] <= TOLERANCE_MM else "bad"
            else:
                c4 = "next" if stage == "confirm" and queue_ and queue_[0] == n else "todo"
            if improved:
                c5 = "ok"
            elif stage == "improve":
                c5 = "next"
            else:
                c5 = "todo"
            if n == names[0]:                                    # a few words beside the box, on the first row
                if stage == "improve":
                    c5 += f"|marker {len(marker_robot) + len(marker_skipped) + 1}/{len(cfg.MARKER_IDS)}"
                elif improved:
                    c5 += f"|{improved.get('after_mm', 0):.1f} mm"
                elif stage == "done":
                    c5 += "|press I"
            rows[n] = [c1, c2, c3, c4, c5]
        return rows

    def next_robot():
        left_ = [n for n in names if n not in robot_ok]
        return left_[0] if left_ else None

    def start_confirm():
        nonlocal stage, queue_
        stage, queue_ = "confirm", list(names)
        confirm_px.clear()
        raw_px.clear()
        off_mm.clear()

    def restart():
        nonlocal stage, queue_, placement, message, accepted, loaded, improved
        stage, queue_, placement, message, accepted = "click", list(names), None, None, False
        loaded = improved = None
        marker_queue.clear()
        marker_robot.clear()
        marker_skipped.clear()
        report.clear()
        for d in (click_px, clicked, raw_px, confirm_px, off_mm, missed):
            d.clear()

    def hint():
        """What to do now, for a key or click that is not part of the current step."""
        if test is not None and test["step"] == "confirm":
            return f"Press Y to move the robot to {test['what']}, or N to cancel."
        if test is not None and test.get("arrived"):
            return "Use D A W S to centre the gripper, then Y = centred (save) or N = leave it."
        if test is not None:
            return "Wait: the robot is moving."
        if stage == "click":
            return f"Step 1: click the centre of square {queue_[0]}."
        if stage == "robot":
            return f"Step 3: press T to check square {next_robot()} with the robot."
        if stage == "confirm":
            return f"Step 4: click the centre of square {queue_[0]} again."
        if stage == "fix":
            return "Press U to correct the square, or R to start again."
        if stage == "failed":
            return "Press R to start again."
        if stage == "improve":
            return f"Step 5: press T to send the robot to marker {marker_queue[0]}."
        return "Step 1.5 is complete. Q = quit, R = calibrate again."

    def marker_test(i):
        """Step 5: the robot hovers over marker i where the current calibration puts it."""
        poses = load_lab5_poses()
        xy = place[0] @ layout[i] + place[1]
        z = max(poses["pick"][n][1][2] for n in names) + MARKER_HOVER_M
        pose = [float(xy[0]), float(xy[1]), z] + list(poses["rpy"])
        for p_ in ([pose[0], pose[1], poses["z_safe"]] + pose[3:], pose):
            check_pose(p_, poses)
        return {"step": "confirm", "name": i, "what": f"marker {i}", "marker": i, "pose": pose,
                "z_safe": poses["z_safe"]}

    def finish_markers():
        """Step 5: fit the layout with A, B, C and the markers the robot visited; keep it only if better."""
        nonlocal place, improved, stage, message, message_colour
        stage = "done"
        ids = [i for i in cfg.MARKER_IDS if i in marker_robot]
        report.clear()
        if not ids:
            message, message_colour = "No marker was measured: calibration kept as it was.", ORANGE
            return
        labels = list(names) + [f"marker {i}" for i in ids]
        src = np.array([clicked[n] for n in names] + [layout[i] for i in ids], float)
        dst = np.array([squares[n] for n in names] + [marker_robot[i] for i in ids], float)
        before = np.linalg.norm(src @ place[0].T + place[1] - dst, axis=1) * 1000
        # Markers far apart: the robot's own scale (its distances vs the ruler-measured layout) can be fitted too
        Rs, ts, after_s = rigid_fit(src, dst, stretch=True)
        scale_pct = (math.hypot(Rs[0, 0], Rs[1, 0]) - 1) * 100
        use_stretch = len(ids) >= MIN_MARKERS_STRETCH and abs(scale_pct) <= MAX_STRETCH_PCT
        R, t, after = (Rs, ts, after_s) if use_stretch else rigid_fit(src, dst)
        print("Step 5, distance left per point (mm), before -> after:")
        for lab, b, a in zip(labels, before, after):
            print(f"  {lab:9s} {b:5.1f} -> {a:5.1f}")
        print(f"  turn {turn_deg(R):+.2f} deg, robot distances / layout distances {scale_pct:+.2f} % "
              f"({'included' if use_stretch else 'not included'})")
        better = after.max() < before.max() and after[:len(names)].max() <= TOLERANCE_MM
        report.extend([f"- Worst distance over A, B, C and {len(ids)} marker(s): {before.max():.1f} mm before, "
                       f"{after.max():.1f} mm after.",
                       "- Per point after: " + ", ".join(f"{lab} {a:.1f}" for lab, a in zip(labels, after)) + " mm"])
        if use_stretch:
            report.append(f"- The robot's distances are {scale_pct:+.1f} % of the marker layout: included in the "
                          "calibration (each robot has its own small scale error).")
        elif abs(scale_pct) > MAX_STRETCH_PCT:
            report.append(f"- Robot and layout distances differ by {scale_pct:+.1f} %: too much to be the robot. Measure "
                          "the markers with a ruler (MARKER_LAYOUT_MM in config.py) and tell the technician.")
        else:
            report.append(f"- Only {len(ids)} marker(s) measured: the robot's scale ({scale_pct:+.1f} %) needs "
                          f"{MIN_MARKERS_STRETCH} or more, so it is not included.")
        if not better:
            message, message_colour = "Step 5 did not improve the fit: calibration kept as it was.", ORANGE
            return
        p_ = {"R": R, "t": t, "turn": turn_deg(R), "left": dict(zip(names, after[:len(names)]))}
        check = json.loads(cfg.MARKERS_FILE.read_text()).get("check")
        save_markers(p_, clicked)
        data = json.loads(cfg.MARKERS_FILE.read_text())
        off = {n: round(float(a), 1) for n, a in zip(names, after)}
        data["check"] = {"time": datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds"), "off_mm": off, "passed": True,
                         "method": "A, B, C and markers centred with the robot (step 5)",
                         "previous": check}
        improved = {"time": datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds"), "markers": ids,
                    "before_mm": round(float(before.max()), 1), "after_mm": round(float(after.max()), 1),
                    "scale_pct": round(scale_pct, 2), "scale_included": bool(use_stretch),
                    "markers_robot_mm": {str(i): [round(float(v) * 1000, 1) for v in marker_robot[i]] for i in ids}}
        data["improved"] = improved
        cfg.MARKERS_FILE.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2))
        project_status(max_age=0)
        place = (R, t)
        off_mm.clear()
        off_mm.update(off)
        message, message_colour = f"Step 5 saved: worst {before.max():.1f} -> {after.max():.1f} mm.", GREEN

    while True:
        frame = cam.read()
        centres, corners, ids = detector.detect(frame)
        view.update(centres)
        shown = frame.copy()
        if ids is not None:
            cv2.aruco.drawDetectedMarkers(shown, corners, ids)
        seen = sum(1 for i in cfg.MARKER_IDS if i in centres)
        ready = view.ready()
        if stage == "improve" and test is None and not marker_queue:
            finish_markers()

            if stage != "done":

            dist, pair = min((distance_to_segment(pt, marker_px[a], marker_px[b]), (a, b)) for a, b in pairs)

        diagonals = [p for p in pairs if marker_px and
                     segments_cross(marker_px[p[0]], marker_px[p[1]],
                                    *[marker_px[i] for i in cfg.MARKER_IDS if i not in p])]
        for a, b in pairs:

                     3 if selected == (a, b) else 2, cv2.LINE_AA)
            t = 0.5 if (a, b) not in diagonals else (0.3 if diagonals.index((a, b)) == 0 else 0.7)

        # ---------------------------------------------------------- two-point measurement
        free_mm = None
        for p_ in point_px:
            cv2.circle(shown, (int(p_[0]), int(p_[1])), 7, BLUE, -1)
        if len(point_px) == 2 and ready:
            p0, p1 = (np.array(view.camera_to_robot(*p_)) for p_ in point_px)
            free_mm = float(np.hypot(*(p0 - p1))) * 1000
            colour = BLUE if free_result is None else (GREEN if free_result[2] else RED)
            cv2.line(shown, tuple(int(v) for v in point_px[0]), tuple(int(v) for v in point_px[1]), colour, 3,
                     cv2.LINE_AA)
            label = f"{free_mm:.1f} mm" if free_result is None else \
                f"{free_mm:.1f} mm / ruler {free_result[0]:g} ({free_result[1]:+.1f})"
            mid = (np.asarray(point_px[0]) + np.asarray(point_px[1])) / 2
            put(shown, label, (mid[0] + 10, mid[1] - 12), colour, 0.7)

        # ---------------------------------------------------------- A, B, C
        if ready:
            fitted = placement is not None and not accepted and stage in ("robot", "fix", "failed")
            if fitted and placement["case"] == "one_square":
                Rr, tr = placement["R_rest"], placement["t_rest"]   # Lab 5 positions placed with the other squares
                for name, xy in squares.items():
                    lx, ly = Rr.T @ (np.asarray(xy) - tr)
                    px, py = view.robot_to_camera(lx, ly)
                    cv2.circle(shown, (int(px), int(py)), 9, RED, 2)
                    put(shown, name, (px + 10, py - 10), RED, 0.6)
                odd = placement["odd"]
                gx, gy = click_px[odd]
                cv2.circle(shown, (int(gx), int(gy)), 13, GREEN, 3, cv2.LINE_AA)
                put(shown, f"{odd} here", (gx + 16, gy + 26), GREEN, 0.6)
            elif fitted:                                             # best fit, shown even though it failed
                for name, xy in squares.items():
                    lx, ly = placement["R"].T @ (np.asarray(xy) - placement["t"])
                    px, py = view.robot_to_camera(lx, ly)
                    cv2.circle(shown, (int(px), int(py)), 9, RED, 2)
                    put(shown, f"{name} {placement['left'][name]:.1f} mm", (px + 10, py - 10), RED, 0.6)
            if place is not None and stage in ("improve", "done"):
                for i in cfg.MARKER_IDS:                             # step 5: robot points on the markers
                    if i in marker_robot:
                        px, py = to_camera(marker_robot[i])
                        cv2.circle(shown, (int(px), int(py)), 7, RED, 2)
                    elif stage == "improve" and marker_queue and marker_queue[0] == i:
                        px, py = to_camera(place[0] @ layout[i] + place[1])
                        cv2.circle(shown, (int(px), int(py)), 16, ORANGE, 3)
                        put(shown, "next", (px + 18, py - 14), ORANGE, 0.6)
            if place is not None and stage != "click" and not fitted:
                for name, xy in squares.items():                     # Lab 5 positions on the picture
                    px, py = to_camera(xy)
                    cv2.circle(shown, (int(px), int(py)), 9, RED, 2)
                    put(shown, name, (px + 10, py - 10), RED, 0.7)
                    if name in off_mm:
                        ok = off_mm[name] <= TOLERANCE_MM
                        put(shown, f"{off_mm[name]:.1f} mm", (px + 12, py + 24), GREEN if ok else RED, 0.6)
            for name, (cx, cy) in (confirm_px if stage in ("confirm", "done") else click_px).items():
                if name in raw_px:
                    ux, uy = raw_px[name]
                    cv2.circle(shown, (int(ux), int(uy)), 3, BLUE, -1)
                    cv2.line(shown, (int(ux), int(uy)), (int(cx), int(cy)), BLUE, 1, cv2.LINE_AA)
                xy = view.camera_to_robot(cx, cy)
                sq = [view.robot_to_camera(xy[0] + dx * HOLE_MM / 2000, xy[1] + dy * HOLE_MM / 2000)
                      for dx, dy in ((-1, -1), (-1, 1), (1, 1), (1, -1))]
                cv2.polylines(shown, [np.int32(sq)], True, GREEN, 1, cv2.LINE_AA)
                cv2.drawMarker(shown, (int(cx), int(cy)), BLUE, cv2.MARKER_CROSS, 18, 2)

        # ---------------------------------------------------------- robot state
        if test is not None and test.get("step") == "sent" and tester is not None:
            if tester.state == "arrived":

        # ---------------------------------------------------------- instruction box
        keys = "- Backspace = redo the previous square    - R = start again    - Q = quit"
        if not squares:

        elif not ready:
            title, colour = f"Markers not found ({seen}/4) - clicks are ignored", RED
            lines = ["- Check that nothing hides a marker: the robot arm, a hand, a cube.",
                     "- Robot arm in the way? Click ROBOT: LEARNING MODE (or press L): it goes to its sleep pose.",

        elif test is not None:

            if test["step"] == "confirm":

                         f"y = {pose[1]:.3f}, z = {pose[2]:.3f}"
                         + (f" ({MARKER_HOVER_M * 1000:.0f} mm above your level-1 pick height)." if "marker" in test
                            else "."),

                         "- Close every other program connected to the robot first."]
            elif tester is not None and test.get("arrived"):
                n = test["name"]

                title, colour = (f"Marker {n}: is the gripper centred over the middle of the marker?" if "marker" in test
                                 else f"Square {n}: is the gripper centred over the hole?"), BLUE
                lines = ["- Stand in front of the robot, at least 30 cm away. Look from the front, then from the side.",
                         "- Not centred? Move it one step per key:  D = your right   A = your left   "
                         "W = away from you   S = towards you",
                         f"- R / F = up / down to look closer (height never saved)   1 / 5 = step 1 or 5 mm "

                         f"- Moved so far: x {dx:+.1f} mm, y {dy:+.1f} mm" + ("  (moving...)" if tester.state == "moving" else ""),

                          f"- Y = centred: save it for {n} (same x, y at every level, pick-up and drop; heights unchanged)"),
                         ("- N = skip this marker" if "marker" in test else "- N = leave it as it was")
                         + "    - L = leave it, robot to sleep pose + learning mode"]
            else:

        elif selected is not None:

            title, colour = f"Type your ruler value for {what}, then press Enter", ORANGE

                     "- " + (message if message_colour == RED else "Backspace = delete     Esc = cancel")]
        elif stage == "click":
            name = queue_[0]

            lines = [f"- Click the centre of hole {name}. The program finds the hole's edges (green outline) and uses its centre.",

                     "- Click the picture first.", keys]

                     "- L = robot to sleep pose with learning mode on, any time."]

        elif stage == "improve":

                     f"- Press T, then Y: the robot hovers {MARKER_HOVER_M * 1000:.0f} mm above marker {i} (orange circle).",
                     "- Centre the gripper over the middle of the marker with D A W S, then Y. N = skip this marker.",

                     "- Keep clear of the robot.    - L = robot to sleep pose + learning mode    - Q = quit"]
        elif stage == "confirm":

                             f"({len(names) - len(queue_) + 1}/{len(names)})"), GREEN
            lines = ["- Each red circle (your Lab 5 position) should sit in the centre of its square.",
                     f"- Click the centre of {name}. Every square within {TOLERANCE_MM:g} mm passes.", keys]
        else:                                                            # done
            offs = ", ".join(f"{n} {d:.1f} mm" for n, d in off_mm.items())
            if max(off_mm.values()) <= TOLERANCE_MM:
                title, colour = (f"Step 1.5 already complete (saved {loaded}): {offs}" if loaded
                                 else f"Step 1.5 complete: {offs}"), GREEN
                lines = list(report) + ["- Next step: python step2_collect_data.py"]
                if not improved:
                    lines.append("- Optional, more accurate: press I. The robot also visits the 4 markers (about 5 min).")
                else:
                    lines.append(f"- Step 5 done ({improved['before_mm']:.1f} -> {improved['after_mm']:.1f} mm"
                                 + (f", robot scale {improved['scale_pct']:+.1f} % included"
                                    if improved.get("scale_included") else "") + "). I = do it again.")
                lines += ["- Optional ruler checks: click a line between two markers, type your ruler value, Enter.",
                          "- R = calibrate again from step 1    - Q = quit"]
            else:
                title, colour = f"Not confirmed: {offs}", RED
                lines = ["- The second clicks do not agree with the first within 5 mm.",
                         "- Press R and do it again, clicking the centre of each hole.", "- Q = quit"]
        if message and message_colour in (RED, GREEN, ORANGE) and selected is None:
            lines = ["- " + message] + lines
        if tester is not None and test is None:
            lines = lines + [f"- {tester.status}"]

        pic = with_progress(shown, "1.5")
        strip = checklist_panel(frame.shape[1], checklist()) if squares else np.full((150, frame.shape[1], 3), 255, np.uint8)
        button, rect = robot_button(pic.shape[1] - frame.shape[1], strip.shape[0],
                                    tester.status if tester is not None else "Robot not connected yet")
        pic = np.vstack([np.hstack([strip, button]), pic])
        shown = instruction_box(pic, title, lines, colour)
        top = shown.shape[0] - pic.shape[0]                              # the button, in window pixels
        button_rect[0] = (frame.shape[1] + rect[0], top + rect[1], frame.shape[1] + rect[2], top + rect[3])

        panel_offset[0] = shown.shape[0] - frame.shape[0]
        picture_width[0] = frame.shape[1]
        display_scale[0] = min(1.0, 1280 / shown.shape[1], 1000 / shown.shape[0])   # fits a 1080p screen
        last_shown = shown
        cv2.imshow(WINDOW, cv2.resize(shown, None, fx=display_scale[0], fy=display_scale[0]))

        # ---------------------------------------------------------- keys
        key = cv2.waitKey(30) & 0xFF
        if button_clicks:                                                # the button = key L
            button_clicks.clear()

            if test is not None and test["step"] == "sent" and not test.get("arrived"):
                message, message_colour = "Wait until the robot has stopped, then press L.", ORANGE
            elif test is not None and test.get("arrived"):               # at a square: leave it, go up and rest
                tester.send("up", list(test["now"]), test["z_safe"])
                message, message_colour = f"{test['what'].capitalize()}: left as it was. Robot going to rest.", ORANGE
                test = None
            else:

                if tester is None or tester.state == "failed":
                    tester = RobotTest()

                message, message_colour = "Robot going to its sleep pose, then learning mode on.", ORANGE
            continue
        if test is not None:                                             # robot keys come first
            if test["step"] == "confirm" and (key == 27 or char in "nN"):
                test = None
            elif test["step"] == "confirm" and char in "yY":
                if tester is None or tester.state == "failed":
                    tester = RobotTest()
