    which: e.g. "Guided pick 2 of 5". A drop correction is saved to the Lab 5 positions of that
    square and level (drop only; a backup of the old file is kept).
    Returns (dx, dy, dz in mm, turn in degrees), "stop" if the student pressed Esc, or None if the
    moves have no descent to the cube followed by close_gripper() (then the caller replays normally)."""
    steps = with_drop_turn(recorder.steps, square, level)
    k = next((i for i, s_ in enumerate(steps) if s_[0] == "move" and s_[1][2] < poses["z_safe"] - 0.001
              and math.hypot(s_[1][0] - cube.x, s_[1][1] - cube.y) < 0.002), None)
    if k is None or k + 1 >= len(steps) or steps[k + 1][0] != "close":
        return None
    down = list(steps[k][1])
    xyz = [down[0], down[1], down[2] + cfg.GUIDED_HOVER_MM / 1000]
    turn = 0.0                                    # degrees, + = anticlockwise seen from above (as cube.angle_deg)
    busy = ["- Keep clear of the robot.", "- Ctrl+C in the Run window = stop"]

    def pose(p_xyz=None, p_turn=None):
        return list(p_xyz or xyz) + list(turned_rpy(down[3:], turn if p_turn is None else p_turn))

    def go(new_xyz, new_turn, what):
        """Move there if it is allowed; returns "" or the reason it did not move."""
        nonlocal xyz, turn
        gap_z = abs(new_xyz[2] - down[2]) if what == "height" else 0.0   # the hover height is not a correction
        if max(abs(new_xyz[0] - down[0]), abs(new_xyz[1] - down[1]), gap_z) * 1000 > cfg.GUIDED_MAX_MM:
            return f"- Not moved: more than {cfg.GUIDED_MAX_MM} mm from where the camera saw the cube."
        if abs(new_turn) > GUIDED_MAX_DEG:
            return f"- Not turned: more than {GUIDED_MAX_DEG} degrees."
        try:
            check_pose(pose(new_xyz, new_turn), poses)
        except ValueError as e:
            return f"- Not moved: {e}"
        try:
            while_busy(run_steps([("move", pose(new_xyz, new_turn))], poses), robot, picture, f"{which}: moving",
                       busy)
        except RuntimeError as e:                 # e.g. the gripper pressed on the cube or the platform
            print(f"  Move refused by the robot: {e}")
            return MOVE_REFUSED
        xyz, turn = list(new_xyz), new_turn
        return ""

    while_busy(run_steps(steps[:k] + [("move", pose())], poses), robot, picture,
               f"{which}: moving above the cube", busy)
    stop_line = "- Esc = stop: nothing is picked, the robot goes back to rest."
    stages = ["move", "turn", "height"]
    stage, note = 0, ""
    while True:
        dx, dy, dz = ((xyz[i] - down[i]) * 1000 for i in range(3))
        names = ["1 Keys: position", "2 Arrows: turn", "3 Arrows: height", "4 Keys: drop position"]
        route = "- Steps:  " + "  ->  ".join(f"[{n}]" if i == stage else n for i, n in enumerate(names)) + \
                "      ENTER = next step"
        if stages[stage] == "move":
            title = f"{which} - step 1 of 4: move the gripper over the MIDDLE of the cube"
            lines = ["- Stand in front of the robot, at least 30 cm away. Look from the front, then from the side.",
                     "- Press D to move it to your RIGHT, A to your LEFT (1 mm each press).",
                     "- Press W to move it AWAY from you, S TOWARDS you (1 mm each press).",
                     f"- Moved so far: {dx:+.0f} mm towards/away, {dy:+.0f} mm right/left.",
                     "- Over the middle? Press ENTER to go to step 2 (turning), also if it was right already.",
                     "- Guided picks teach the robot its corrections; they are NOT counted in your success rate.",
                     stop_line]
            allowed, hint = "wasd", "Use W, A, S, D to move, then ENTER."
        elif stages[stage] == "turn":
            title = f"{which} - step 2 of 4: turn the gripper to line up with the cube"
            lines = ["- Look from at least 30 cm: the fingers should be parallel to two sides of the cube.",
                     "- Press the LEFT arrow to turn anticlockwise, the RIGHT arrow to turn clockwise (2 degrees each).",
                     f"- Turned so far: {turn:+.0f} degrees.",
                     "- Lined up? Press ENTER: the gripper goes down to the grip height (it does not close yet).",
                     stop_line]
            allowed, hint = ("left", "right"), "Use the LEFT and RIGHT arrows to turn, then ENTER."
        else:
            title = f"{which} - step 3 of 4: check the height before it grips"
            lines = ["- The fingers should be around the middle of the cube: not pressing on its top, not touching "
                     "the platform.",
                     "- Press the UP arrow to go up, the DOWN arrow to go down (1 mm each press).",
                     f"- Height changed so far: {dz:+.0f} mm.",
                     "- Right height? Press ENTER: the gripper closes and carries the cube to the square, where it "
                     "stops again (step 4).", stop_line]
            allowed, hint = ("up", "down"), "Use the UP and DOWN arrows, then ENTER."
        key = ask_step(picture, title, [route] + lines + (note.split("\n") if note else []), set(allowed) | {"enter", "esc"},
                       hint)
        note = ""
        if key == "esc":
            while_busy(run_steps([("move", xyz[:2] + [poses["z_safe"]] + pose()[3:])], poses, then_rest=True), robot,
                       picture, "Stopped: moving up, then to the sleep pose", busy)
            return "stop"
        if key == "enter":
            if stages[stage] == "height":
                break
            stage += 1
            if stages[stage] == "height":                       # down to the grip height
                note = go([xyz[0], xyz[1], down[2]], turn, "height")
                if note == MOVE_REFUSED:                         # a finger landed on the cube: back up, step 1 again
                    try:
                        while_busy(run_steps([("move", pose())], poses), robot, picture, f"{which}: moving back up",
                                   busy)
                    except RuntimeError as e:
                        print(f"  Move refused by the robot: {e}")
                    stage = 0
                    note = ("- The robot STOPPED on the way down: a finger landed on the cube. It went back up.\n"
                            "  Move it over the MIDDLE of the cube again (W/A/S/D), then ENTER.")
            continue
        mm, deg = 0.001, 2.0                  # standing in front of the robot: towards you = +x, your right = +y
        new = list(xyz)
        if key == "s":
            new[0] += mm
        elif key == "w":
            new[0] -= mm
        elif key == "d":
            new[1] += mm
        elif key == "a":
            new[1] -= mm
        elif key == "up":
            new[2] += mm
        elif key == "down":
            new[2] -= mm
        new_turn = turn + (deg if key == "left" else -deg if key == "right" else 0.0)
        note = go(new, new_turn, stages[stage])
    corr = [xyz[i] - down[i] for i in range(3)]
    rest_steps = [("close",)]
    for s_ in steps[k + 2:]:                   # the moves at the cube (e.g. back up) get the same correction
        if s_[0] == "move" and math.hypot(s_[1][0] - cube.x, s_[1][1] - cube.y) < 0.002:
            s_ = ("move", [s_[1][0] + corr[0], s_[1][1] + corr[1], s_[1][2]] + pose()[3:])
        rest_steps.append(s_)
    moving = ["- " + target, "- Ctrl+C in the Run window = stop (power switch for an emergency)"]
    result = (corr[0] * 1000, corr[1] * 1000, corr[2] * 1000, turn)

    # ---- step 4: stop just above the drop position (the move before open_gripper())
    d = next((i for i, s_ in enumerate(rest_steps) if s_[0] == "open"), None)
    if d is None or d == 0 or rest_steps[d - 1][0] != "move":
        while_busy(run_steps(rest_steps, poses, then_rest=True), robot, picture, "Robot moving - keep clear", moving)
        return result
    drop = list(rest_steps[d - 1][1])
    dxy = [drop[0], drop[1]]
    dturn = 0.0                                   # extra turn at the drop, degrees (+ = anticlockwise from above)
    hover = drop[2] + GUIDED_DROP_HOVER_MM / 1000

    def drop_pose(xy, z, t):
        return list(xy) + [z] + list(turned_rpy(drop[3:], t))
    while_busy(run_steps(rest_steps[:d - 1] + [("move", drop_pose(dxy, hover, dturn))], poses), robot, picture,
               "Robot moving to the square - keep clear", moving)
    note = ""
    while True:
        ddx, ddy = (dxy[0] - drop[0]) * 1000, (dxy[1] - drop[1]) * 1000
        route = "- Steps:  " + "  ->  ".join(n if i < 3 else f"[{n}]" for i, n in enumerate(names)) + \
                "      ENTER = drop"
        title = f"{which} - step 4 of 4: is the cube right above square {square}?"
        lines = [route,
                 f"- The cube is {GUIDED_DROP_HOVER_MM} mm above where it will be let go (square {square}, level {level}).",
                 "- From at least 30 cm, look from the front, then from the side: is it centred over the square?",
                 "- Press D to move it to your RIGHT, A to your LEFT (1 mm each press).",
                 "- Press W to move it AWAY from you, S TOWARDS you (1 mm each press).",
                 "- Press the LEFT arrow to turn it anticlockwise, the RIGHT arrow clockwise (2 degrees each), so it "
                 "lines up with the square.",
                 f"- Changed so far: {ddx:+.0f} mm towards/away, {ddy:+.0f} mm right/left, turn {dturn:+.0f} degrees.",
                 f"- Lined up? Press ENTER: it goes down and lets go. Changes are saved for square {square}, every "
                 "level.",
                 "- Esc = no change: drop at the saved position."]
        key = ask_step(picture, title, lines + (note.split("\n") if note else []),
                       {"w", "a", "s", "d", "left", "right", "enter", "esc"},
                       "Use W, A, S, D to move, LEFT / RIGHT arrows to turn, then ENTER.")
        note = ""
        if key == "esc":
            dxy, dturn = [drop[0], drop[1]], 0.0
            break
        if key == "enter":
            break
        st = 0.001
        new = list(dxy)
        new[0] += {"s": st, "w": -st}.get(key, 0.0)
        new[1] += {"d": st, "a": -st}.get(key, 0.0)
        new_turn = dturn + {"left": 2.0, "right": -2.0}.get(key, 0.0)
        if max(abs(new[0] - drop[0]), abs(new[1] - drop[1])) * 1000 > cfg.GUIDED_MAX_MM:
            note = f"- Not moved: more than {cfg.GUIDED_MAX_MM} mm from the saved drop position."
            continue
        if abs(new_turn) > GUIDED_MAX_DEG:
            note = f"- Not turned: more than {GUIDED_MAX_DEG} degrees."
            continue
        try:
            check_pose(drop_pose(new, hover, new_turn), poses)
        except ValueError as e:
            note = f"- Not moved: {e}"
            continue
        try:
            while_busy(run_steps([("move", drop_pose(new, hover, new_turn))], poses), robot, picture,
                       f"{which}: moving", busy)
        except RuntimeError as e:
            print(f"  Move refused by the robot: {e}")
            note = MOVE_REFUSED
            continue
        dxy, dturn = new, new_turn
    shift = [dxy[0] - drop[0], dxy[1] - drop[1]]
    tail = [("move", drop_pose(dxy, drop[2], dturn))]
    for s_ in rest_steps[d:]:                  # the moves at the square (e.g. back up) get the same shift and turn
        if s_[0] == "move" and math.hypot(s_[1][0] - drop[0], s_[1][1] - drop[1]) < 0.002:
            s_ = ("move", [s_[1][0] + shift[0], s_[1][1] + shift[1], s_[1][2]] + list(turned_rpy(s_[1][3:], dturn)))
        tail.append(s_)
    while_busy(run_steps(tail, poses, then_rest=True), robot, picture, "Robot moving - keep clear", moving)
    if max(abs(shift[0]), abs(shift[1])) >= 0.0005:
        save_drop_xy(square, level, dxy, poses)
        print(f"  Drop position of square {square} (every level) moved by x {shift[0] * 1000:+.0f} mm, "
              f"y {shift[1] * 1000:+.0f} mm (saved in {cfg.LAB5_FILE.name}, old file kept as a backup)")
    if abs(dturn) >= 1:
        turns = load_drop_turns()
        total = turns.get(square, turns.get(f"{square} {level}", 0.0)) + dturn
        save_drop_turn(square, total)
        print(f"  Drop turn of square {square} (every level): {dturn:+.0f} deg, now {total:+.0f} deg in total "
              f"(saved in {DROP_TURN_FILE.name})")
    return result


DROP_TURN_FILE = cfg.CALIB_DIR / "drop_turn.json"        # guided picks, step 4: gripper turn at each drop


def load_drop_turns():
    try:
        return json.loads(DROP_TURN_FILE.read_text())
    except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError):
        return {}


def with_drop_turn(steps, square, level):
    """The recorded steps with the saved turn for this drop (square, level) added at the drop: the move
    before open_gripper() and the moves at the same place after it."""
    turns = load_drop_turns()
    turn = turns.get(square, turns.get(f"{square} {level}", 0.0))       # one turn per square (all levels)
    c = next((i for i, s_ in enumerate(steps) if s_[0] == "close"), len(steps))
    d = next((i for i, s_ in enumerate(steps) if s_[0] == "open" and i > c), None)   # the open after the grip
    if not turn or d is None or d == 0 or steps[d - 1][0] != "move":
        return list(steps)
    drop = steps[d - 1][1]
    out = list(steps)
    for i in range(c, len(out)):              # every move at the drop place, from above it to back up
        s_ = out[i]
        if s_[0] == "move" and math.hypot(s_[1][0] - drop[0], s_[1][1] - drop[1]) < 0.002:
            out[i] = ("move", list(s_[1][:3]) + list(turned_rpy(s_[1][3:], turn)))
    return out


def save_drop_turn(square, turn):
    turns = {k: v for k, v in load_drop_turns().items() if not k.startswith(square)}   # old per-level entries
    turns[square] = round(float(turn), 1)
    cfg.CALIB_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    DROP_TURN_FILE.write_text(json.dumps(turns, indent=2))


MOVE_REFUSED = ("- The robot STOPPED: the gripper pressed on something (the cube or the platform),\n"
                "  or the wrist could not turn there. Move back (e.g. the UP arrow) and try smaller steps.")


def save_drop_xy(square, level, xy, poses):
    """Save a new x, y for the DROP positions of one square at EVERY level (a stack is vertical: only
    the heights differ, and they are not changed), with a backup of the old file. Pick positions are
    not changed, so step 1.5 stays ticked. level: the level where it was corrected (marked tested)."""
    data = read_lab5_file()
    for lv in data["drop"][square]:
        old = data["drop"][square][lv]
        data["drop"][square][lv] = [round(float(xy[0]), 4), round(float(xy[1]), 4), old[2]]
        poses["drop"][square][lv] = list(data["drop"][square][lv])        # used from the next pick on
    data["tested"][f"drop {square} {level}"] = "ok"
    backup = f"lab5_positions_backup_{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M%S')}.json"
    shutil.copy(cfg.LAB5_FILE, cfg.CALIB_DIR / backup)
    save_lab5_file(data)


VOICE_WORDS = ("Voice words:  red / yellow / green = sort only that colour,  all = every colour,  "
               "go = pick,  skip = leave it,  stop = end")


def ask_voice(voice, cam_img, title, colour, expected, say, sorting, timeout=None):
    """Voice extra: wait for one of the expected words, keeping the window alive.
    The screen shows what to say now, the last word heard and all the voice words.
    Words said before this question (e.g. during a robot move) are ignored. Returns the word, or
    None after timeout seconds."""
    start = time.time()
    ignored = None
    while timeout is None or time.time() - start < timeout:
        last = voice.last_heard[0] if voice.last_heard else None
        note = f'  - "{ignored}" is not used here' if ignored and last == ignored else ""
        show_status(cam_img, title, [f"SAY: {say}      (sorting now: {sorting or 'all colours'})",
                                     voice.heard_text() + note, VOICE_WORDS], colour, refresh=False)
        word = voice.get(since=start)
        if word in expected:
            print(f"  Voice: {word}")
            return word
        if word:
            ignored = word
            print(f'  Voice: "{word}" ignored here (expected: {", ".join(expected)})')
        cv2.waitKey(50)
    return None


def gripper_turns(steps, poses):
    """From the recorded moves: how far (degrees) the gripper is turned, relative to your Lab 5 yaw,
    where it closes on the cube and where it opens over the square. None if not found."""
    base = _rotation(poses["rpy"])

    def turn_before(index):
        for kind, *rest in reversed(steps[:index]):
            if kind == "move":
                r = _rotation(rest[0][3:]) @ base.T            # the turn from the Lab 5 orientation
                return math.degrees(math.atan2(r[1, 0], r[0, 0]))
        return None
    kinds = [st[0] for st in steps]
    if "close" not in kinds or "open" not in kinds:
        return None, None
    close_i = kinds.index("close")
    open_i = len(kinds) - 1 - kinds[::-1].index("open")
    return turn_before(close_i), turn_before(open_i)


def turn_text(cube, at_cube, at_square):
    """One line for the window and the Run window: cube angle and what the gripper does about it."""
    if at_cube is None:
        return f"cube turned {cube.angle_deg:+.0f} deg"
    text = (f"cube turned {cube.angle_deg:+.0f} deg; gripper turns {at_cube:+.0f} deg at the cube, "
            f"{at_square:+.0f} deg at the square")
    if abs(cube.angle_deg) > 5 and abs(at_cube) < 1:
        text += ("  (no turn: USE_ORIENTATION is False in config.py)" if not cfg.USE_ORIENTATION
                 else "  (no turn: pick_and_drop() does not use cube.angle_deg)")
    return text

"""
Test how to turn the gripper so it lines up with a turned cube (step 4, Level 2).

    python test_wrist_turn.py

The robot goes above square A at the safe height with your Lab 5 orientation, then
tries three ways of turning the gripper by +30 degrees, going back to straight after each:

    1. yaw + 30 deg       2. roll + 30 deg       3. the wrist joint (joint 6) + 30 deg

After each one, answer in this window: did the gripper turn about the vertical, and which way?
At the end it tells you what to set in config.py (TURN_AXIS).
Keep clear of the robot; the power switch is the emergency stop.
"""
import math

from robot import NiryoRobot, load_lab5_poses, orientation_gap_deg

TURN_DEG = 30


def ask(question, answers):
    while True:
        a = input(question).strip().lower()
        if a in answers:
            return a
        print("  Please type one of:", ", ".join(answers))


def report(robot, asked_rpy=None):
    pose, joints = robot.get_pose(), robot.get_joints()
    print(f"  robot reports roll, pitch, yaw = {[round(v, 3) for v in pose[3:]]}"
          f"   joint 6 = {math.degrees(joints[5]):.1f} deg")
    if asked_rpy is not None:
        gap = orientation_gap_deg(asked_rpy, pose[3:])
        print(f"  difference from the orientation asked for: {gap:.1f} deg"
              + ("  <- the robot did NOT go to it" if gap > 5 else ""))
    return pose, joints


def main():
    poses = load_lab5_poses()
    roll, pitch, yaw = poses["rpy"]
    x, y, _ = poses["pick"]["A"][1]
    z = poses["z_safe"]
    a = math.radians(TURN_DEG)
    print(f"Lab 5 orientation: roll {roll:.3f}, pitch {pitch:.3f}, yaw {yaw:.3f} rad")
    if abs(abs(pitch) - math.pi / 2) > 0.15:
        print("  Note: pitch is not close to 1.57 rad, so the gripper does not point straight down.\n"
              "  Turning yaw or roll then also tilts the gripper. Consider re-teaching Lab 5 with pitch about 1.57.")

    robot = NiryoRobot()
    robot.start()
    results = {}
    try:
        straight = [x, y, z, roll, pitch, yaw]
        tests = [("yaw", [x, y, z, roll, pitch, yaw + a]),
                 ("roll", [x, y, z, roll + a, pitch, yaw])]
        print("\nGoing above square A, straight (your Lab 5 orientation)...")
        robot.move_pose(*straight)
        _, j_straight = report(robot, straight[3:])
        input("Look at the gripper from above. Press Enter to try the first turn...")

        for name, pose in tests:
            print(f"\nTest: {name} + {TURN_DEG} deg")
            robot.move_pose(*pose)
            report(robot, pose[3:])
            results[name] = ask("Did the gripper turn about the vertical? c = clockwise (seen from above), "
                                "a = anticlockwise, n = no turn, t = it tilted instead: ", ["c", "a", "n", "t"])
            robot.move_pose(*straight)

        print(f"\nTest: wrist joint (joint 6) + {TURN_DEG} deg")
        j = list(j_straight)
        j[5] += a
        robot.move_joints(j)
        pose6, _ = report(robot)
        results["joint6"] = ask("Did the gripper turn about the vertical? c = clockwise, a = anticlockwise, "
                                "n = no turn: ", ["c", "a", "n"])
        robot.move_pose(*straight)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        print("\nStopped.")
    finally:
        robot.finish()

    print("\nResults:", results)
    for axis in ("yaw", "roll"):
        if results.get(axis) in ("c", "a"):
            print(f"\nUse {axis}. In config.py set:\n    TURN_AXIS = \"{axis}\"\n"
                  "Keep YAW_SIGN = 1. Then watch one turned cube in step 4: the gripper should line up with its "
                  "sides.")
            return
    if results.get("joint6") in ("c", "a"):
        print("\nOnly the wrist joint turned the gripper. Send these lines to your lab technician:"
              f"\n  Lab 5 rpy {[round(v, 3) for v in (roll, pitch, yaw)]}; after joint 6 + {TURN_DEG} deg "
              f"the robot reports rpy {[round(v, 3) for v in pose6[3:]]}")
    else:
        print("\nNo test turned the gripper: check the robot and its Lab 5 orientation with your lab technician.")

    main()

"""
STEP 4.3 - Summarise your robot trials against the specification.

    python trials_summary.py

Reads results/trials.csv (written by step4_sort_blocks.py) and prints, for the real
robot runs (dry runs and guided picks, which you corrected with the keys, are left out):
  - pick success rate (cubes placed correctly), with a 95 % confidence interval
  - wrong-colour drops and the other failure causes (you give the cause when you answer
    n after a pick), with the upper limit of the true rate when none happened
  - time per cube
  - grip offsets with and without the parallax correction (from --measure-offset)
It also saves the summary to results/trials_summary.txt for your report.
"""
import csv
from datetime import datetime
from statistics import mean, stdev

import config as cfg
from progress import print_progress


def wilson(successes, n, z=1.96):
    """95 % confidence interval of a proportion (Wilson score interval): (low, high)."""
    if n == 0:
        return 0.0, 1.0
    p = successes / n
    centre = (p + z * z / (2 * n)) / (1 + z * z / n)
    half = z * ((p * (1 - p) / n + z * z / (4 * n * n)) ** 0.5) / (1 + z * z / n)
    return max(0.0, centre - half), min(1.0, centre + half)


def rate_text(successes, n):
    if n == 0:
        return "no data"
    low, high = wilson(successes, n)
    return f"{successes}/{n} = {successes / n:.0%}  (95 % interval {low:.0%} to {high:.0%})"


def main():
    path = cfg.RESULTS_DIR / "trials.csv"
    if not path.exists():
        raise SystemExit("No results/trials.csv yet: run step4_sort_blocks.py with the robot first.")
    with open(path, newline="") as f:
        real = [r for r in csv.DictReader(f) if r.get("dry_run") != "True"]
    # Guided picks were corrected with the keys: they show how much correcting was needed, not how well the
    # robot does on its own, so they are reported separately and left out of every rate below.
    guided = [r for r in real if r.get("guided") == "True"]
    rows = [r for r in real if r.get("guided") != "True"]
    if not rows:
        raise SystemExit("No unguided robot picks yet: the first picks of each run are guided (corrected with the keys) "
                         "and do not count. Run step4_sort_blocks.py for more picks.")

    answered = [r for r in rows if r.get("outcome") in ("y", "n")]
    placed = sum(r["outcome"] == "y" for r in answered)
    wrong = sum(r.get("failure_cause") == "wrong colour" for r in answered)
    g_ok = sum(r.get("outcome") == "y" for r in guided)
    lines = [f"Robot trials: {len(rows)} picks by the robot on its own ({len(answered)} with an answer to "
             f"'placed correctly?')",
             f"Guided picks (corrected with the keys, NOT counted below): {len(guided)}, {g_ok} placed correctly", "",
             f"Pick success (R5):        {rate_text(placed, len(answered))}"]

    lines.append(f"Wrong-colour drops (R4):  {rate_text(wrong, len(answered))}")
    if wrong == 0 and answered:
        lines.append(f"  (0 wrong does not prove the rate is 0: with {len(answered)} picks it can still be up to "
                     f"{wilson(0, len(answered))[1]:.0%})")
    causes = {}
    for r in answered:
        if r["outcome"] == "n":
            causes[r.get("failure_cause") or "not recorded"] = causes.get(r.get("failure_cause") or "not recorded", 0) + 1
    if causes:
        lines.append("Failures by cause:        " + ", ".join(f"{c} {n}" for c, n in sorted(causes.items())))

    times = sorted(datetime.fromisoformat(r["time"]) for r in rows)
    gaps = [(b - a).total_seconds() for a, b in zip(times, times[1:]) if (b - a).total_seconds() < 120]
    if gaps:
        lines.append(f"Time per cube (R8):       {mean(gaps):.1f} s on average ({len(gaps)} intervals; "
                     f"gaps over 2 minutes are left out as breaks)")

    for corrected in ("False", "True"):
        offsets = []
        for r in rows:
            try:
                if r.get("parallax_corrected") == corrected and r.get("offset_mm", "").strip():
                    offsets.append(float(r["offset_mm"]))
            except ValueError:
                pass
        label = "with" if corrected == "True" else "without"
        if len(offsets) >= 2:
            lines.append(f"Grip offset {label:7s} parallax correction (R6): {mean(offsets):.1f} mm average, "
                         f"standard deviation {stdev(offsets):.1f} mm, {len(offsets)} picks")
        elif offsets:
            lines.append(f"Grip offset {label:7s} parallax correction (R6): {offsets[0]:.1f} mm (1 pick)")

    colours = {}
    for r in answered:
        colours.setdefault(r["label"], []).append(r["outcome"] == "y")
    lines += ["", "Success by colour:"]
    lines += [f"  {c:7s} {rate_text(sum(v), len(v))}" for c, v in sorted(colours.items())]

    text = "\n".join(lines)
    print(text)
    cfg.RESULTS_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    (cfg.RESULTS_DIR / "trials_summary.txt").write_text(text)
    print("\nSaved results/trials_summary.txt")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print_progress("4:Robot trials")
    main()

import cv2
import numpy as np

GREEN, RED, BLUE, ORANGE, GREY = (0, 160, 0), (0, 0, 220), (200, 80, 0), (0, 140, 255), (90, 90, 90)


def instruction_box(image, title, lines=(), colour=BLUE):
    """Return the image with a white instruction panel ABOVE it (nothing on the picture is covered):
    a coloured title and grey lines. The picture starts at row panel_height(...) of the result."""
    shown = image.copy()
    if shown.ndim == 2:
        shown = cv2.cvtColor(shown, cv2.COLOR_GRAY2BGR)
    h, w = shown.shape[:2]
    size, title_h, line_h, box_h = _panel_sizes(w, len(lines))
    panel = np.full((box_h, w, 3), 255, np.uint8)
    cv2.rectangle(panel, (0, 0), (w - 1, box_h - 1), colour, 4)
    cv2.putText(panel, title, (12, int(36 * size)), cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 1.05 * size, colour,
                max(2, int(3 * size)), cv2.LINE_AA)
    for n, line in enumerate(lines):
        cv2.putText(panel, line, (12, title_h + line_h * n + int(22 * size)), cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX,
                    0.7 * size, (40, 40, 40), 2, cv2.LINE_AA)
    return np.vstack([panel, shown])


def _panel_sizes(width, n_lines):
    size = max(0.55, min(1.0, width / 1280))          # smaller text on small images
    title_h, line_h = int(48 * size), int(32 * size)
    return size, title_h, line_h, title_h + line_h * n_lines + int(14 * size)


def panel_height(width, n_lines):
    """Height of the panel instruction_box adds above an image of this width."""
    return _panel_sizes(width, n_lines)[3]

"""
The complete vision pipeline: camera frame in, list of classified cubes out.

    frame -> find ArUco markers -> top-down view -> find cube candidates
          -> trained model predicts colour + confidence -> robot x, y
"""
import math
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

import cv2
import numpy as np

import config as cfg


def parallax_corrected(x, y):
    from mapping import check_parallax, correct_parallax
    if cfg.CAMERA_POSITION_M is None:
        raise SystemExit("USE_PARALLAX_CORRECTION is True but CAMERA_POSITION_M in config.py is not measured yet")
    check_parallax()
    return correct_parallax(x, y, cfg.PARALLAX_HEIGHT_MM / 1000.0, cfg.CAMERA_POSITION_M)
from aruco_view import MarkerDetector, TopDownView, load_marker_positions
from block_finder import find_cubes, load_background
from robot import load_lab5_poses, square_centres

COLOURS_BGR = dict(cfg.CLASS_DRAW_BGR, **{"?": (255, 255, 255)})


@dataclass
class Detection:
    label: str
    confidence: float
    x: float              # robot coordinates, metres
    y: float
    angle_deg: float      # cube turn in the ROBOT frame, -45 to +45 (+ = anticlockwise from above)
    u: float              # top-down pixel
    v: float
    box: np.ndarray
    crop: np.ndarray


@dataclass
class VisionResult:
    detections: list = field(default_factory=list)
    topdown: np.ndarray = None
    mask: np.ndarray = None
    markers_seen: int = 0
    fresh: bool = False     # all 4 markers seen in THIS frame
    inference_ms: float = 0.0


class VisionSystem:
    def __init__(self, model=None, use_background=True):
        self.markers = MarkerDetector()
        self.view = TopDownView(load_marker_positions())
        self._exclude_target_squares()
        self.background = load_background() if use_background else None
        self.model = model
        self._last_marker_draw = None

    def _exclude_target_squares(self):
        """Cubes stacked on A, B and C must never be picked up again."""
        try:
            poses = load_lab5_poses()
        except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError) as e:
            print(f"Warning: squares A, B, C not excluded from the pick zone ({e})")
            return
        self.view.keep_out(list(square_centres(poses).values()))

    def process(self, frame):
        result = VisionResult()
        centres, corners, ids = self.markers.detect(frame)
        self._last_marker_draw = (corners, ids)
        result.markers_seen = sum(1 for i in cfg.MARKER_IDS if i in centres)
        result.fresh = self.view.update(centres)
        if not self.view.ready():
            return result

        result.topdown = self.view.warp(frame)
        candidates, result.mask = find_cubes(result.topdown, self.view, self.background)

        start = time.perf_counter()
        if self.model is not None:
            labels, confs = self.model.predict([c.crop for c in candidates])
        else:
            labels, confs = ["?"] * len(candidates), [0.0] * len(candidates)
        result.inference_ms = (time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000.0

        for c, label, conf in zip(candidates, labels, confs):
            x, y = self.view.topdown_to_robot(c.u, c.v)
            if cfg.USE_PARALLAX_CORRECTION:                   # step 4: KEY PART in mapping.py
                x, y = parallax_corrected(x, y)
            result.detections.append(Detection(label, conf, x, y, self.robot_angle(c),
                                               c.u, c.v, c.box, c.crop))
        return result

    def robot_angle(self, c):
        """The cube's turn in the ROBOT frame (degrees, -45 to +45, + = anticlockwise seen from above).
        The top-down picture is flipped compared with the robot (right = -y, down = -x), so an
        angle measured in the picture cannot be used directly: convert two points along an edge."""
        a = math.radians(c.angle_deg)
        x0, y0 = self.view.topdown_to_robot(c.u, c.v)
        x1, y1 = self.view.topdown_to_robot(c.u + 10 * math.cos(a), c.v + 10 * math.sin(a))
        angle = math.degrees(math.atan2(y1 - y0, x1 - x0))
        return (angle + 45.0) % 90.0 - 45.0                 # a cube looks the same every 90 degrees

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ drawing
    def draw(self, frame, result):
        """Return (camera image, top-down image) with markers, zone and detections drawn."""
        cam = frame.copy()
        corners, ids = self._last_marker_draw
        if ids is not None:
            cv2.aruco.drawDetectedMarkers(cam, corners, ids)
        status = f"markers {result.markers_seen}/4" + ("" if result.fresh else "  (NOT all visible)")
        cv2.putText(cam, status, (10, 30), cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.8,
                    (0, 255, 0) if result.fresh else (0, 0, 255), 2)
        if result.topdown is None:
            return cam, None

        top = result.topdown.copy()
        # RETR_LIST: the outer edge and the holes (the circles round A, B and C inside the zone)
        contours, _ = cv2.findContours(self.view.zone_mask, cv2.RETR_LIST, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE)
        cv2.drawContours(top, contours, -1, (255, 255, 255), 1)
        # The same pick-zone outline on the camera picture: put cubes inside it.
        for c in contours:
            pts = [self.view.robot_to_camera(*self.view.topdown_to_robot(float(u), float(v))) for u, v in c[:, 0]]
            cv2.polylines(cam, [np.int32(pts)], True, (255, 255, 255), 2, cv2.LINE_AA)
        for d in result.detections:
            colour = COLOURS_BGR.get(d.label, (255, 255, 255))
            cv2.drawContours(top, [np.int32(d.box)], 0, colour, 2)
            # No model yet (step 2): every found object is just "object", ready to be labelled.
            text = "object" if self.model is None else f"{d.label} {d.confidence:.2f}"
            where = f"x {d.x * 1000:.0f}  y {d.y * 1000:.0f} mm"
            label(top, [text], (int(d.u) - 30, int(d.v) - 24), colour, 0.45)
            box = [self.view.robot_to_camera(*self.view.topdown_to_robot(float(u), float(v))) for u, v in d.box]
            cv2.polylines(cam, [np.int32(box)], True, colour, 3, cv2.LINE_AA)
            px, py = np.min(np.array(box), axis=0)
            label(cam, [text, where], (px, py - 6), colour, 0.45)
        return cam, top


def label(image, lines, org, colour, size=0.6):
    """Black text on a white tag, with a border in the predicted colour, so it is readable on any
    background. org = bottom-left of the tag; the tag is moved down if it would leave the image."""
    font, thick, pad = cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 1, 4
    sizes = [cv2.getTextSize(t, font, size, thick)[0] for t in lines]
    w = max(sz[0] for sz in sizes) + 2 * pad
    line_h = max(sz[1] for sz in sizes) + 6
    h = line_h * len(lines) + pad
    x, y = int(org[0]), int(org[1])
    x = max(0, min(x, image.shape[1] - w - 1))
    y = max(h + 1, y)
    cv2.rectangle(image, (x, y - h), (x + w, y), (255, 255, 255), -1)
    cv2.rectangle(image, (x, y - h), (x + w, y), colour, 2)
    for i, t in enumerate(lines):
        cv2.putText(image, t, (x + pad, y - h + line_h * (i + 1) - 2), font, size, (0, 0, 0), thick + 1,
                    cv2.LINE_AA)


def show(name, image, max_width=960):
    """imshow that shrinks big images to fit the screen."""
    if image is None:
        return
    h, w = image.shape[:2]
    if w > max_width:
        image = cv2.resize(image, (max_width, int(h * max_width / w)))
    cv2.imshow(name, image)

"""
OPTIONAL EXTRA - Voice commands (speech recognition, offline).

Try it on its own first:
    python voice_commands.py

Say one of the words in WORDS. Each word the program recognises is printed.

Setup (once):
  1. Install the packages into your project's virtual environment:
         pip install vosk sounddevice
  2. Download the small English model "vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15" (about 40 MB)
     from https://alphacephei.com/vosk/models and unzip it into this folder, so that
     the folder vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15 sits next to this file.
  3. Plug in a microphone (a USB headset works best in a noisy lab).

How it works: Vosk is a neural-network speech recogniser that runs on your PC,
with no internet. Giving it a short list of words (a "grammar") makes it much
more reliable: it only has to decide WHICH of these words you said.

In your sorting program:
    from voice_commands import VoiceListener
    voice = VoiceListener()          # starts listening in the background
    word = voice.get()               # the newest word said, or None (never waits)
    voice.stop()

Safety: a voice command is only read BETWEEN robot moves. It is not an
emergency stop: the emergency stop is the robot's power switch.
"""
import json
import queue
import threading
import time
from pathlib import Path

# The words the recogniser listens for. Add or remove words here.
WORDS = ["red", "yellow", "green", "all", "go", "skip", "stop"]
HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
SMALL_MODEL = "vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15"        # recommended: 40 MB, loads in seconds


def find_model():
    """The small model if it is here, otherwise any other vosk-model-* folder next to this file."""
    if (HERE / SMALL_MODEL).exists():
        return HERE / SMALL_MODEL
    others = sorted(p for p in HERE.glob("vosk-model-*") if p.is_dir())
    return others[0] if others else HERE / SMALL_MODEL


MODEL_DIR = find_model()
SAMPLE_RATE = 16000


class VoiceListener:
    """Listens to the microphone in a background thread and keeps the recognised words."""

    def __init__(self, words=WORDS, model_dir=MODEL_DIR, device=None):
        try:
            import sounddevice
            import vosk
        except ImportError:
            raise SystemExit("Voice commands need two packages: pip install vosk sounddevice")
        if not Path(model_dir).exists():
            raise SystemExit(f"Speech model not found: {model_dir}\n"
                             f"Download vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15 from https://alphacephei.com/vosk/models "
                             f"and unzip it next to voice_commands.py")
        vosk.SetLogLevel(-1)
        self.words = list(words)
        name = Path(model_dir).name
        print(f"Loading the speech model {name}..." +
              ("" if "small" in name else " (a large model: this can take a minute or more)"))
        model = vosk.Model(str(model_dir))
        if "small" in name:
            # Small models accept a word list ("grammar"): they only decide WHICH of these words was said.
            grammar = json.dumps(self.words + ["[unk]"])      # [unk] = anything else
            self._recogniser = vosk.KaldiRecognizer(model, SAMPLE_RATE, grammar)
        else:
            # Large models cannot take a word list: they hear any English, and only our words are kept below.
            self._recogniser = vosk.KaldiRecognizer(model, SAMPLE_RATE)
        print("Speech model ready.")
        self._audio = queue.Queue()
        self._words = queue.Queue()                 # (word, time) for each command word
        self.last_heard = None                       # (text, time, is_command): for the display
        self._running = True
        self._stream = sounddevice.RawInputStream(samplerate=SAMPLE_RATE, blocksize=8000, dtype="int16",
                                                  channels=1, device=device,
                                                  callback=lambda data, *_: self._audio.put(bytes(data)))
        self._stream.start()
        self._thread = threading.Thread(target=self._listen, daemon=True)
        self._thread.start()

    def _listen(self):
        while self._running:
            try:
                data = self._audio.get(timeout=0.5)
            except queue.Empty:
                continue
            if self._recogniser.AcceptWaveform(data):
                text = json.loads(self._recogniser.Result()).get("text", "").strip()
                if not text:
                    continue
                now = time.time()
                commands = [w for w in text.split() if w in self.words]
                for word in commands:
                    self._words.put((word, now))
                self.last_heard = (commands[-1] if commands else text, now, bool(commands))

    def get(self, since=None):
        """The newest command word, or None. Never waits; older unread words are dropped.
        since = a time.time() value: words heard before it are ignored (e.g. said during a robot move)."""
        word = None
        while not self._words.empty():
            w, t = self._words.get_nowait()
            if since is None or t >= since:
                word = w
        return word

    def heard_text(self):
        """One line for the screen: the last thing heard and how long ago."""
        if self.last_heard is None:
            return "Heard: nothing yet"
        text, t, is_command = self.last_heard
        ago = f"{time.time() - t:.0f} s ago"
        if is_command:
            return f'Heard: "{text}" ({ago})'
        if text == "[unk]":
            return f"Heard: something that is not a command ({ago})"
        return f'Heard: "{text}" - not a command ({ago})'


    def stop(self):
        self._running = False
        self._stream.stop()
        self._stream.close()


def main():
    voice = VoiceListener()
    print("Listening for:", ", ".join(WORDS), "  (Ctrl+C to stop)")
    try:
        while True:
            word, _ = voice._words.get()                       # wait for the next word
            print("heard:", word)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    finally:
        voice.stop()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

           # different values for each axis

    print(" Niryo 1 Robot Control Program")

    # Connect to your robot (ROBOT at the top of this file)
    n1 = NiryoOneClient()

    n1.set_learning_mode(True)

    n1.move_pose(x, y, z, r, p, ya)
    # stay in the while loop below
    while True:


        if keyboard.read_key()=="x":
           x=x+incr
        elif keyboard.read_key()=="c":
            x=x-incr

            y=y+incr
        elif keyboard.read_key()=="u":

        elif keyboard.read_key()=="z":

            n1.open_gripper(RobotTool.GRIPPER_1, 1000)
